## BUG-0460 — BUG-0446 and BUG-0454 are fixed: the education student and American opportunity credit tests read their answers in order

- **Caught by:** BUG-0446 and BUG-0454, recorded open; this entry closes both because the inventory is append-only.
- **Source:** `forms/2025/person.yaml` and `forms/2025/dependent.yaml`. `edu_student` was `all[f8863.paid, edu, TIN (person: tin or itin_applied), edu_1098t]` (dependent: with `claimed` second), and `edu_aoc` was `all[edu_student, edu_line23 No, edu_line24 Yes, edu_line25 No, edu_line26 No, household.all_tin, edu_ein]`. Under spec 4.7.2 an `all` remembers an unknown conjunct and goes on, and a later `false` decides it, leaving what the unknown conjunct read reachable and unanswered.
- **Symptom:** as recorded in BUG-0446 (`edu_line23`) and BUG-0454 (`person.edu`). BUG-0446 reproduced on the pre-fix tree with `ny.status.qss.200000` in a seeded random order: complete while `dependent[daughter].edu_line23` was unanswered and reachable, with `edu_line24` Yes and `edu_line25` Yes deciding `edu_aoc` false past it. The same structure leaks lines 24 to 26, `edu` and `f8863.paid` past any later deciding conjunct, in both forms.
- **Fix:** both tests are nested chooses in their own order (the bank order). `edu_student`: f8863.paid, then `edu`, then the TIN (person: `tin`, else `itin_applied`; dependent: `claimed` before `edu`), then the Form 1098-T answer. `edu_aoc`: `edu_student`, then line 23 (Yes stops), line 24 (No stops), line 25 (Yes stops), line 26 (Yes stops), then `household.all_tin`, then the EIN answer. Each level is a helper line, and every stop is `edu_no` (year parameter `edu.no`, false). A choose with an unknown guard restores the memo (spec 4.7.3), so no later question is reached past an unanswered one. The interview-rules baseline entry `person.edu` is removed.
- **Fix lines:** `person.edu_student`, `person.edu_student_edu`, `person.edu_student_tin`, `person.edu_student_itin`, `person.edu_aoc`, `person.edu_aoc23`, `person.edu_aoc24`, `person.edu_aoc25`, `person.edu_aoc26`, `person.edu_aoc_tin`, `person.edu_no`, `dependent.edu_student`, `dependent.edu_student_claimed`, `dependent.edu_student_edu`, `dependent.edu_student_tin`, `dependent.edu_aoc`, `dependent.edu_aoc23`, `dependent.edu_aoc24`, `dependent.edu_aoc25`, `dependent.edu_aoc26`, `dependent.edu_aoc_tin`, `dependent.edu_no`
- **Siblings checked:** `dependent.claimed_no_tin`, `dependent.ctc_child`, `dependent.edu_adj`, `dependent.edu_aoc`, `dependent.edu_aoc23`, `dependent.edu_aoc24`, `dependent.edu_aoc25`, `dependent.edu_aoc26`, `dependent.edu_aoc_tin`, `dependent.edu_line27`, `dependent.edu_line28`, `dependent.edu_line29`, `dependent.edu_line30`, `dependent.edu_llc`, `dependent.edu_no`, `dependent.edu_over_refused`, `dependent.edu_show24`, `dependent.edu_show25`, `dependent.edu_show26`, `dependent.edu_student`, `dependent.edu_student_claimed`, `dependent.edu_student_edu`, `dependent.edu_student_tin`, `dependent.odc_person`, `household.id_count`, `household.tin_count`, `person.edu_adj`, `person.edu_aoc`, `person.edu_aoc23`, `person.edu_aoc24`, `person.edu_aoc25`, `person.edu_aoc26`, `person.edu_aoc_tin`, `person.edu_line27`, `person.edu_line28`, `person.edu_line29`, `person.edu_line30`, `person.edu_llc`, `person.edu_llc_tin_refused`, `person.edu_no`, `person.edu_over_refused`, `person.edu_show24`, `person.edu_show25`, `person.edu_show26`, `person.edu_student`, `person.edu_student_edu`, `person.edu_student_itin`, `person.edu_student_tin` (generated by the sibling tool; no change was needed in any: the edu_show24 to edu_show26, edu_llc and edu_over_refused tests are conjunctions too, and the structural leak prototype lists no input released through them after this change)
- **Regression predictions:** no recorded value changes (a nested choice in the conjunction's own order is equal on every complete return).
- **Validation:** every federal (1,641) and New York (338) fixture passes unchanged, so no partial fixture's decided value became unknown and none needed completing. `tools/structural_leaks.mjs` lists `edu`, `edu_line23` to `edu_line26` and `f8863.paid` before the change and none of them after. interview-rules with an empty baseline. The transcription, render, class M and completeness reviews of person and dependent were rerun. The tier run of this change.
- **Tags:** interview; leak; nested-choose; fixed

## BUG-0461 — Form 8863 line 31 evaluates the course-materials input for the record, leaving it reachable at completion

- **Caught by:** `tools/structural_leaks.mjs` (binding reads), 2026-11-07; reproduced in a seeded random answering order of `ny.status.qss.200000` (complete with `person[taxpayer].edu_mat`, and in another order `dependent[daughter].edu_mat`, reachable and unanswered).
- **Source:** `forms/2025/person.yaml` and `forms/2025/dependent.yaml`, `edu_line31`: the lifetime learning credit alternative instantiates `aqee` at `ws4_llc` with `mat: edu_mat`, and `ws4_llc` reads only `inst` and `adj`. A def instance evaluates every binding in the caller's frame (spec 4.7.4), so `edu_mat` is reached and never needed there. Where `edu_aoc` is false, line 30 (which needs it) takes `zero`, and nothing else reads it.
- **Symptom:** the interview reports complete while the American-opportunity-only course-materials question is reachable and unanswered. No value is affected.
- **Disposition:** open, low: bind only the parameters the instance's line reads (for example a second def or an `ws4_llc` instance without `mat`), or have the evaluator skip bindings the line does not read (an evaluator change in both evaluators). Not held in the interview-rules baseline: the sampled orders do not show it on main.
- **Tags:** interview; leak; def-binding; open

## BUG-0463 — interview-rules' random traversal answered from the fixture's whole answer map, so leftover answers hid order-dependent leaks

- **Date:** 2026-11-08
- **Caught by:** reading (Gemini 4 Argon, docs/ARGON_CLAUDE_DISCUSSION.md MSG-007), confirmed in MSG-008 and reproduced on d41235c4 (T-258).
- **Source:** `engine/src/interview-rules.ts` at d41235c4, line 211: the `random` task called `walk(data, config, c.inputs, ...)`, where the reversed and shuffled replays use `replayed(config, w.events)`.
- **Symptom:** a random answering order that reaches an input the bank-order walk never asks was answered from the fixture's leftover value (for example a `0` kept after its gate was closed), so the error the task prints for that case ("asks X, which the answers in bank order never reach") could fire only for an input missing from the fixture altogether. Measured on d41235c4: 0 failures over the 82 random traversals as run; with `replayed(config, w.events)` and the walk otherwise unchanged, 3 New York fixtures fail on `f8960.allocated_taxes`.
- **Why it survived:** the check was green, and a green check over leftover answers looks the same as a green check without them.
- **Disposition:** fixed (tool only; no form lines): the random traversal answers only what the bank-order walk asked (`replayed(config, w.events)`); the fixture's other answers are withheld. Fixed with BUG-0464.
- **Tags:** interview-rules; check-weakness; masked-by-fixture; fixed

## BUG-0464 — interview-rules' walk offered only answered questions, so a random order could never reach a question its answers lacked

- **Date:** 2026-11-08
- **Caught by:** reading (Gemini 4 Argon, MSG-014, failure mode 1), reproduced on d41235c4 (T-258).
- **Source:** `engine/src/interview-rules.ts` at d41235c4, `walk()`: line 86 filtered the open questions to those `answers` holds, and line 88 checked only the interview's own next question (the first reachable in bank order).
- **Symptom:** an input reachable at some state, but only out of bank order, was never picked by a random traversal, so order-dependent leaks went unseen. MSG-014 states that fixing BUG-0463 alone catches nothing; measured, it catches 1 template (`f8960.allocated_taxes`, 3 cases). With both fixed, plus a scan of every incomplete state of the bank-order walk, 59 templates are reached only out of bank order (54 by the scan, 5 more by the random traversals).
- **Disposition:** fixed (tool only; no form lines): while the return is incomplete every reachable unanswered input is open; a pick the answers lack throws Unanswered in bank order and is reported (and the pick made again) in a random traversal. The walk records each input reachable at an incomplete state that a later answer hid before it was asked. On a complete return those inputs, and those a random traversal reaches, fail unless held in `order_dependent_reach` of `tools/interview_rules_baseline.json`, seeded with today's 59, each with its reason. Refused returns keep the old behaviour (questions open at a refusal are not leaks). Minimal returns (every gate closed; each existence gate opened alone) and planted-fault self-tests were added in the same change.
- **Tags:** interview-rules; check-weakness; order-dependence; fixed

No value is affected: `eic.eligible` is false either way.

## BUG-0466 — 59 input templates are reachable only out of bank order, and 11 are asked in bank order and then unread

- **Date:** 2026-11-08
- **Caught by:** interview-rules after BUG-0463 and BUG-0464 were fixed (T-258).
- **Source:** conjunctions (`all`/`any` tests, collection sums with conjunctive `where`, refusal gates evaluated before their lines) whose deciding operand is answered after another operand's question becomes reachable. Each template and the line it is read under are listed with their reasons in `order_dependent_reach` and `walked_unused` of `tools/interview_rules_baseline.json`; the families are the EIC steps, the dependent qualifying-child and qualifying-relative tests, the education credit tests, the saver's credit and IRA tests, Form 5695, the household marital tests, the New York estimated-tax penalty and use-tax tests, and single conjunctions in Schedule 1, Schedule A, Form 4952, Form 8863 and the sales rows.

No value is affected; asking a reachable question is allowed, so the cost is questions.

## BUG-0467 — interview-rules' random traversal reported an out-of-order input only when its pick landed on it

- **Date:** 2026-11-08
- **Caught by:** review (Gemini 4 Argon, docs/ARGON_CLAUDE_DISCUSSION.md MSG-017), reproduced: with every unanswered input open at an incomplete state reported, the existing single seed finds `ny_it201.ask.spouse_resident` (first ny.schedule.single.65000) and `f8960.allocated_taxes` (ny.worksheet.mfj.400000), and also `f8962.married_in_2025` (generated.0), none held.
- **Source:** `engine/src/interview-rules.ts`, `walk()` as committed for BUG-0464: with `reach`, an input the answers lack was reported only when `pick` chose it, so at a state with many open inputs it was usually passed over. The self-test's `plantLeak` appended its refusal after the target's own refusals, so `scope.ready`'s unknown `scope.credits` refusal (index 1) stopped evaluation before it, and 3 of 15 planted leaks were reachable in no order.
- **Symptom:** order-dependent leaks seen in a traversal's states went unreported; the F2 strength measurement read 12 of 15 where the plants, not the check, were at fault.
- **Disposition:** fixed (tool only; no form lines): at each incomplete state of a traversal every unanswered open input is reported and the pick is made among the answered ones; `plantLeak` puts its refusal first; random traversals run 5 seeds per chosen walk. The three templates are held in `order_dependent_reach` (62 entries); they are conjunctions on the filing status or `sa.itemizes`, open questions of BUG-0466's kind.
- **Tags:** interview-rules; check-weakness; sampling; fixed

## BUG-0468 — eic.zero is a compared line with a line subject and no verdict section, and the review store did not check it

- **Date:** 2026-11-09
- **Caught by:** the year-carry control (store design 2.3), then `review_store.py check` strengthened to compare each index's line subjects with its verdict sections.
- **Source:** `reviews/2025/transcription/eic.index.json`. `household.yaml` began reading `eic.zero` (gate `household.eic_disallowed_claim`, 2026-11-03), which made this helper line a compared line of the eic transcription review. The next line-scoped pass (2026-11-04, the line 4 pass) rewrote the whole line-subject table, adding an `eic.zero` row, but reviewed no section for it. The committed log before the store migration already had the row and no section, so the migration did not cause it. `subjects.index_state` compares subjects only, so the recorded row made the line read as current. The same strengthened check also flags `transcription/div.deepseek` (optional family): its verdict section `div.screen` has no line subject, and its log is stale for the lines now compared.
- **Symptom:** the eic transcription review records no verdict on `eic.zero` (a helper whose expression is the parameter `sales.zero`, cited at i1040gi p. 42, Step 5, worksheet lines 2 and 4) while its index says every compared line is current.
- **Disposition:** the check is fixed: `review_store.py check` fails when an index has a line subject without a verdict section or the reverse, in every kind and family, federal and New York (self-test `test_a_line_subject_without_a_verdict_fails_the_store_check`). Held, not fixed: both gaps are listed with their reasons in the shrink-only `SUBJECT_VERDICT_EXCEPTIONS` of `tools/transcription/review_store.py`; closing `eic.zero` needs a line-scoped transcription review (a paid call, not run). The entry leaves the list when that review lands; the check fails if a listed index no longer has a gap.
- **Tags:** review-store; check-weakness; subjects; eic; open

## BUG-0469 — carry.py judged every log with a line-scoped pass stale once its whole-form subject was out of date

- **Date:** 2026-11-09
- **Caught by:** the eic.zero line-scoped review (BUG-0468): rerun_all.py's carry left all 17 reader disagreements open as "the log is stale; rerun first" while check_logs.py called the log current.
- **Source:** `tools/transcription/carry.py` `plan` compared the first `| subject sha256 |` row of the log (the header's, from the last whole-form review) with the form's current subject. A line-scoped pass records its own subject further down and leaves the header as it was, so after any change to the form every later line-scoped log read as stale. `subjects.log_state`, which check_logs.py uses, judges such a log line by line.
- **Symptom:** no repeat disagreement was carried after a line-scoped review of a form that had changed since its whole review; each was left for adjudication.
- **Disposition:** fixed: against the working tree carry asks `subjects.log_state` (`log_is_current`); against a commit or an in-memory snapshot it keeps the whole-form subject comparison, which can refuse a current log but never accepts a stale one. Self-test `test_against_the_working_tree_currency_is_log_state` fails on the old code. On eic it then carried 5 of 17. Not checked: which earlier line-scoped reviews left carriable disagreements to adjudication because of this.
- **Closes:** BUG-0468 for `transcription/eic` (eic.zero): the line-scoped review (pass a55b2baf366f) AGREEs on `eic.zero`, and `transcription/eic` has left `SUBJECT_VERDICT_EXCEPTIONS`. The pass's scope took in the 17 lines that read `eic.zero`: 5 rulings carried once this bug was fixed, 12 adjudicated, all project stands. `transcription/div.deepseek` stays held under BUG-0468.
- **Tags:** carry; subjects; line-scoped; tool; fixed

## BUG-0470 — Review scope rows join line keys with ", ", which some keys contain, and three readers split on it

- **Date:** 2026-11-09
- **Caught by:** the eic adjudication after the eic.zero review: triage.py refused every section of pass a55b2baf366f.
- **Source:** `transcribe.py` and `render_compare.py` write `| review scope | lines <k1>, <k2>, ... |`. Printed-line keys such as `(Step 5, 1)` contain ", ". `triage.py` (`names = scope[...].split(", ")`) and `audit_transcription.py` (split on "," and strip) refuse the pass as naming unknown lines. `review_store.py` (writing records) splits the same way without failing: the broken pieces enter the record's identity, so fixing the split changes the hash of every stored record whose scope holds such a key.
- **Symptom:** triage and the transcription audit cannot read a line-scoped pass whose scope includes a key with a comma; review-store record identities hold split key fragments.
- **Disposition:** open. The eic rulings of pass a55b2baf366f were stamped from triage run with only that split patched in memory (`.transcription/triage/2025/eic.json`); rerun triage on eic when this is fixed and compare. Fix: an unambiguous scope format (or parse against the form's keys) in the writers and all three readers, and a store migration for the records whose identity changes; count the affected records first.
- **Tags:** review-store; triage; line-scoped; tool; open

## BUG-0471 — BUG-0466 in part: conjunctions rewritten as nested choose in their operands' order; four families held by asserted fixtures

- **Symptom:** as recorded in BUG-0466.

With the operands in their original order, a complete return's value is unchanged: an `all` and its chain stop at the same first false or refused operand. ## BUG-0472 — A wage-only debtor in a chapter 11 bankruptcy case is not asked about it

- **Date:** 2026-11-09
- **Caught by:** standing completeness review (claim f1040#1), adjudicated in the gate-wave review round; the claim's ruling in `reviews/2025/completeness/rulings.json` cites this entry.
- **Source:** i1040gi p. 23, Chapter 11 Bankruptcy Cases: "If you are a debtor in a chapter 11 bankruptcy case, income taxable to the bankruptcy estate and reported on the estate's income tax return includes: Earnings from services you performed after the beginning of the case (both wages and self-employment income); and Income from property described in section 541 ... Because this income is taxable to the estate, don't include this income on your own individual income tax return." and "you (or the trustee if one is appointed) must allocate between you and the bankruptcy estate the wages, salary, or other compensation and withheld income tax reported to you on Form W-2. A similar allocation is required for income and withheld income tax reported to you on Forms 1099."
- **Symptom:** a debtor in a chapter 11 case with only Form W-2 wages (and/or interest, dividends or other Form 1099 income) is never asked about the case. Line 1a is the full W-2 box 1 total and line 25a the full withholding, though the post-petition wages, the estate-property income and the matching withholding belong on the estate's return. The return is accepted with too much income and withholding.
- **Where:** the chapter 11 question exists only in `person.se_screen` (forms/2025/person.yaml, refusing Schedule SE) and the Schedule C screens (forms/2025/sc.yaml); both are reached only with self-employment income. `scope.other_income` (forms/2025/scope.yaml) says it is "not about" wages, interest, dividends or Form 1099-R income, so a wage-only debtor answers No. Readers: `f1040.line1a`, `f1040.line2b`/`3b`, `f1040.line25a`/`25b`, and everything after total income.
- **Witness (executed):** fixture `stage8.single.phaseout.partial` (single, W-2 wages only) evaluates with `f1040.line1a` = $215,300, `f1040.line24` = $39,656.70, `scope.ready` true; setting `person[taxpayer].se_screen` true changes nothing (no Schedule C, so the only chapter 11 question has no effect). No input can mark the return as a chapter 11 debtor's.
- **Proposed fix:** add "being a debtor in a chapter 11 bankruptcy case" to a return-level screen that every filer answers (for example the "Other income or return treatment" list of `scope.other_income`), citing i1040gi p. 23, Chapter 11 Bankruptcy Cases; the allocation (Notice 2006-83) is outside the tool.
- **Severity:** low (rare situation for an individual wage earner; amount-affecting when it occurs).
- **Tags:** unasked-condition; amount-affecting; caught-by-completeness-review; open

## BUG-0473 — The taxpayer's SSN question omits the DHS-authorization condition (Schedule 1-A and the credits that read it)

- **Date:** 2026-11-09
- **Caught by:** standing completeness review (claim s1a#2), adjudicated in the gate-wave review round; the claim's ruling in `reviews/2025/completeness/rulings.json` cites this entry.
- **Source:** i1040gi p. 104, Valid SSN for No Tax on Tips: "However, if 'Valid for Work Only with DHS Authorization' is printed on your social security card, your SSN is valid only as long as the DHS authorization is valid." Pages 108 (overtime) and 110 (seniors) incorporate it ("For more information, see Valid SSN for No Tax on Tips, earlier").
- **Symptom:** `person.work_ssn` asks "Do you have an SSN valid for employment, issued before the due date of your 2025 return (including extensions)?" without the DHS condition. A filer whose card carries the DHS legend and whose authorization has lapsed reads the card's "Valid for Work" and answers Yes. The return then gets the tips, overtime and senior deductions, and the child tax credit through the same question. `dependent.work_ssn` already carries the condition (BUG-0215); the person question does not.
- **Where:** `forms/2025/person.yaml`, `person.work_ssn` (read by `s1a.tip_ssn_count`, `s1a.ot_ssn_count`, `s1a.senior_count`, `household.taxpayer_work_ssn_count` and the CTC counts).
- **Witness (executed):** `stage12.tips.one_employer` with `person.work_ssn` Yes gives `s1a.line13` = $8,000 and `f1040.line13b` = $8,000. When the authorization has lapsed the source gives $0, the value `stage12.tips.no_valid_ssn` produces.
- **Fix sketch:** add the `dependent.work_ssn` wording to the question: answer Yes only if the DHS authorization is still valid.
- **Tags:** question-incomplete; caught-by-completeness-review; open

## BUG-0474 — Working-capital interest is left out of the section 179 business income limit

- **Date:** 2026-11-09
- **Caught by:** standing completeness review (claim s179#3), adjudicated in the gate-wave review round; the claim's ruling in `reviews/2025/completeness/rulings.json` cites this entry.
- **Source:** p946 p. 19: "Net income or loss from a trade or business includes the following items. • Section 1231 gains (or losses). • Interest from working capital of your trade or business. • Wages, salaries, tips, or other pay earned as an employee." i4562 p. 5, Line 11.
- **Symptom:** `s179.income` is `s179.income_sc` (Schedule C line 31 before section 179) plus `f1040.line1a`. The business's working-capital interest is reported as interest income (Schedule B / Form 1040 line 2b) and never enters the limit. When line 11 binds, the tool allows too little section 179 deduction this year and carries too much forward. Section 1231 gains and NOL deductions are refused (scope.schedule1, s1.line8_other) and passive businesses are refused (sc.passive through sc.screened); only the interest item is open.
- **Where:** `forms/2025/s179.yaml`, `s179.income` / `s179.income_sc`; no question separates the business's working-capital interest from other interest.
- **Witness (executed):** `stage14.s179.income_limit` with `$interest=["bank_a"]` and `interest[bank_a].amount=100000` ($1,000 interest on the business's operating account) gives `s179.line11` $3,000, `s179.line12` $3,000 and `s179.line13` $7,000. The source gives line 11 and line 12 $4,000 and line 13 $6,000.
- **Fix sketch:** ask, when the return has both a section 179 election and interest, how much of the interest is from the business's working capital, and add it to `s179.income`. Alternatively, refuse that case.
- **Tags:** amount-affecting (low; understatement of the deduction); question-incomplete; caught-by-completeness-review; open

## BUG-0475 — Home utilities, rent, insurance and repairs are not excluded from Schedule C Part II with the simplified method

- **Date:** 2026-11-09
- **Caught by:** standing completeness review (claim sc#3), adjudicated in the gate-wave review round; the claim's ruling in `reviews/2025/completeness/rulings.json` cites this entry.
- **Source:** i1040sc p. 10: "The simplified method is an alternative to the calculation, allocation, and substantiation of actual expenses." i1040sc p. 14: "Use Part II of Schedule C to deduct business expenses that are unrelated to the qualified business use of the home (for example, expenses for advertising, wages, or supplies, or depreciation of equipment or furniture)."
- **Symptom:** the questions for `sc.line16a`, `sc.line16b` and `sc.line23` exclude home mortgage interest and home real estate taxes. The questions for `sc.line25` ("Utility expenses of the business only"), `sc.line20b` ("Rent for other business property, such as office space"), `sc.line15` (insurance) and `sc.line21` (repairs) do not exclude the home's share. A filer who uses the simplified method can therefore deduct the business share of home utilities, rent, insurance or repairs in Part II as well as the $5-per-square-foot amount on line 30. The only other method, Form 8829, is refused, so every accepted home-office return uses the simplified method.
- **Where:** `forms/2025/sc.yaml`, `sc.line15`, `sc.line20b`, `sc.line21`, `sc.line25` (questions); possibly a note on `sc.ho_uses`.
- **Witness (executed):** `stage14.ho.basic` with `person[taxpayer].sc[home].line25=60000` ($600 of home utilities entered as business utilities) gives `line30` $1,000 and `line31` $18,400. The source gives $19,000, because the home's utilities are not deductible beyond line 30.
- **Fix sketch:** add "not expenses of your home (utilities, rent, insurance, repairs), which the simplified method on line 30 replaces" to those four questions when `sc.ho_uses` is Yes, or unconditionally.
- **Tags:** question-incomplete; amount-affecting; caught-by-completeness-review; open

## BUG-0476 — A market discount bond or contingent payment debt instrument sold with no taxable Schedule B income is neither asked about nor refused

- **Date:** 2026-11-09
- **Caught by:** standing completeness review (claim sales#1), adjudicated in the gate-wave review round; the claim's ruling in `reviews/2025/completeness/rulings.json` cites this entry.
- **Source:** i8949 p. 11 (Worksheet for code "D", market discount: "This is the amount of your gain that is ordinary income. Enter it as a negative amount (in parentheses) in Form 8949, column (g). Also, report it as interest income on your tax return."); i8949 p. 5 / i1040sd p. 5 ("If you sell a taxable contingent payment debt instrument subject to the noncontingent bond method at a gain, your gain is ordinary income (interest income)"; "the Ordinary box in box 2 on Form 1099-B is checked ... an adjustment may be required").
- **Symptom:** only `sb.unsupported` names accrued market discount and contingent payment debt instruments, and it is reached only through `sb.unsupported_if_income`, which is false unless taxable interest, ordinary dividends or capital gain distributions are above zero (`sb.has_income`). On the Form 8949 (detail) route, `sales.code` offers none/B/W/BW/other with code E as its only example, and `sales.special` does not ask about market discount, a contingent payment debt instrument or the Form 1099-B Ordinary box. So a filer whose only income from the bond is the sale gain answers none and the whole gain is computed as capital gain. It should be partly or wholly interest income, taxed at ordinary rates.
- **Where:** forms/2025/sales.yaml (`sales.code`, `sales.special`); forms/2025/sb.yaml (`sb.unsupported_if_income`).
- **Witness (executed):** fixture `sales.box.D` (one long-term sale, $4,000 gain, no interest or dividends) with `sb.unsupported=true`: `sb.has_income` false, `sb.unsupported_if_income` false, no refusal; `sd.line16` = `f1040.line7a` = $4,000, `f1040.line2b` = $0. Realistic case: a tax-exempt municipal bond bought at a market discount and sold at a gain, with accrued market discount in Form 1099-B box 1f and only tax-exempt interest for the year.
- **Proposed disposition:** open, low. Ask, per sale or in `sales.special`, about accrued market discount (box 1f), a contingent payment debt instrument, or a checked Ordinary box, and refuse; or ask `sb.unsupported` whether or not Schedule B income is above zero. Rerun the sales (or sb) completeness and screen reviews. This is related to BUG-0436 (the same question, `sales.code`, leaves out other adjustments) but has a different cause.
- **Tags:** completeness; question-incomplete; open

## BUG-0479 — A line-scoped transcription catalog left out the sales collection that the scoped Schedule D lines sum over

- **Date:** 2026-11-09
- **Caught by:** adjudication of the line-scoped transcription review of `sd` (pass e771f73e2296, receipt `.transcription/sd.lines-c9db5685c8a4`), run for the BUG-0471 sibling check: the reply wrote `{"const": 0}` for 22 of the 24 open Schedule D column lines, noting "the sales collection fields are not supplied".
- **Symptom:** the scoped prompt's "Keyed collections" list is empty: the `sales` collection (its box, route, proceeds, cost and adjustment fields), which every scoped line 1a to 10, columns (d), (e), (g), (h), sums over, is not in the catalog. Only `sales.special`, a screening input, appears. The earlier scoped pass 3c1e462d90db of the same log listed the collection. The reply therefore could not express the lines, and triage reports value differences on completed returns (for example 1b(d): 52, project $61,051.00 against the reply's $0.00 on classm.clcw26.2.deepseek) that are artefacts of the review, not of the encoding.
- **Root cause (read from the code, not traced in a run):** `catalog_selection` in `tools/transcription/transcribe.py`, line-scoped federal branch: "a collection named only as a form is not listed", and a form named only as a form is kept whole only where the scoped lines' citations name its IRS form (`federal_whole(cited)`). The scoped Schedule D lines cite f1040sd, not Form 8949, so `sales` (Form 8949) is dropped although the lines' own expressions read it.
- **Where:** `tools/transcription/transcribe.py`, `catalog_selection` (and `collection_notes(fid, selected)`, which lists only selected collections).
- **Fix sketch:** always list a collection, with its fields, that the scoped lines (or the helpers in their reach) read through `sum_over`, whatever the text names; add a self-test with the sd column lines. Then rerun the line-scoped transcription of sd lines 1a to 10 (paid, owner's call).
- **Disposition:** open. The 24 sd sections of this pass are ruled interface gap citing this entry; the project's lines stand (no HEAD-to-current difference on any sd line over 1,702 fixtures and 500 generated returns).
- **Tags:** review-tool; line-scoped; catalog; interface-gap; open

## BUG-0480 — BUG-0479 is fixed: a line-scoped transcription catalog lists every collection its scoped lines sum over

- **Date:** 2026-11-10
- **Caught by:** the T-150 sibling refresh of BUG-0471 (sd lines 1a to 10 reviewed with no keyed collection in the catalog).
- **Source:** `catalog_selection` (tools/transcription/transcribe.py): in a line-scoped federal review, a collection the excerpt names only as a form was dropped unless the scoped lines' citations named its IRS form; nothing checked whether the scoped lines sum over it.
- **Symptom:** the sd line-scoped prompt listed no `sales` fields, so the second transcription wrote zero placeholders for every column sum.
- **Disposition:** fixed. `collections_read` collects the collections a document's lines read; the line-scoped federal branch keeps such a collection and adds any not otherwise selected (`SUMMED_COLLECTION`). Self-test `LineScopedCatalog` fails on the old code. The sd lines were reviewed again with `sales` in the catalog ($0.45): 32 disagreements, all the known digital-asset widening (T-003): 4 carried, 28 ruled scope, no value difference.
- **Closes:** BUG-0479.
- **Tags:** transcription; catalog; line-scoped; tool; fixed

## BUG-0482 — BUG-0474 is fixed: interest from the business's working capital counts toward the section 179 business income limit

- **Date:** 2026-11-10
- **Closes:** BUG-0474
- **Caught by:** BUG-0474, recorded open; this entry closes it because the inventory is append-only.
- **Source:** p946 p. 19, Taxable income, "Net income or loss from a trade or business includes the following items" and "Interest from working capital of your trade or business"; i4562 p. 5, Line 11.
- **Symptom:** as recorded in BUG-0474.
- **Fix:** asked, not refused. `s179.wc_interest` asks how much of the taxable interest on Form 1040 line 2b is interest from the working capital of a business the filer (or spouse, on a joint return) actively conducts. It is gated (`s179.wc_interest_if_limited`, through `s179.wc_ask`, a nested choose): asked only when line 11 is the business income (`s179.income_binds`: a section 179 deduction is figured, lines 9 and 10 above zero (`s179.has179`), and the business income before it, `s179.income_wages`, Schedule C income before section 179 plus line 1a, is less than line 5 (`s179.income_below5`)) and line 2b is above zero (`s179.has_interest`); otherwise zero. The interest belongs on line 11 whenever line 11 is the business income, even where line 12 is the same, so the question is not limited to returns whose deduction it changes (the render review of this round found the narrower first gate left printed line 11 short). `s179.income` adds it. An answer above line 2b is refused at `s179.income` (`s179.wc_over`, read only where the question is asked, so a refusal of line 2b does not reach the section 179 lines of a return that is not asked; its conflict explanation is in `interview/conflict_checks-2025.yaml`, its place in `tools/coverage/tree.json`).
- **Fix lines:** `s179.income`, `s179.wc_interest`
- **Siblings checked:** `s179.wc_interest_if_limited` (generated; the input's gate line, new here)
- **Regression predictions:** no recorded value changes. Nine complete-return fixtures with a Schedule C, a section 179 deduction and interest now reach the new question (`classm.f1040.4`, `classm.f8962.2`, `classm.sa.3`, `classm.asset.1`, `classm.sc.2`, `classm.f1040.4.deepseek`, `classm.eic.2.deepseek`, `mutation.t2.person.simple_nonelective_excess`) or would read it on a line they do not assert (`classm.f4952.2`, `classm.person.15`, `classm.clcw.4`, `classm.f4952.2.deepseek`, `classm.clcw.4.deepseek`, `classm.person.1.deepseek`); each gains the answer `s179.wc_interest: 0` (its interest is not described as business working capital), and none of their asserted values changes. The test-data default is 0.
- **Validation:** fixtures `bug0474.s179.wc_interest` (the BUG-0474 witness: line 11 and line 12 $4,000, line 13 $6,000), `bug0474.s179.wc_interest_part` ($400 of $1,000: line 11 $3,400, line 13 $6,600), `bug0474.s179.wc_interest_over` (refusal), `bug0474.s179.interest_line11_only` (wages keep line 12 at lines 9 and 10, and line 11 still takes the interest: $12,000), `bug0474.s179.wc_interest_carryover_only` (a carryover with no 2025 property: asked) and `bug0474.s179.income_above_line5` (business income above line 5: not asked, the recorded answer unread), each predicted by hand before recording; every existing fixture passes; interview-rules and mutation clean.
- **Tags:** amount-affecting; question-incomplete; fixed

## BUG-0484 — BUG-0476 is fixed: a sale of a market discount bond or contingent payment debt instrument is refused through its adjustment code

- **Date:** 2026-11-10
- **Closes:** BUG-0476
- **Caught by:** BUG-0476, recorded open; this entry closes it because the inventory is append-only.
- **Source:** i8949 p. 11, Worksheet for Accrued Market Discount Adjustment in Column (g), "reporting the sale or retirement of a market discount bond, enter code “D” for the transaction in column (f)"; i8949 p. 12, Worksheet for Contingent Payment Debt Instrument Adjustment in Column (g), code "O"; i8949 p. 10, the Ordinary box tip; i1040sd p. 4, Market Discount Bonds.
- **Symptom:** as recorded in BUG-0476.
- **Fix:** refused, through the per-sale adjustment question. `sales.code` now names code D (the sale or retirement of a bond or other debt instrument with accrued market discount, such as an amount in Form 1099-B box 1f, whose gain is interest income up to that discount even if the bond's interest is tax-exempt) and code O (a taxable contingent payment debt instrument, such as one reported with the Ordinary box in box 2 checked) as codes to answer other. Other is refused by `sales.bad_code` ("Only applicable B and W adjustments are supported. Review the required code and prepare the unsupported adjustment."), whatever the Schedule B income, so the case no longer depends on `sb.unsupported_if_income`. `sales.special` was not used: its refusal's remedy names only the special gains worksheets, and changing it would change 35 asserted refusals; the aggregate route already excludes box 1f adjustments and the Ordinary box (`sales.aggregate_eligible`).
- **Fix lines:** `sales.code`
- **Siblings checked:** `sales.aggregate_fails`, `sales.bad_code`, `sales.has_b`, `sales.has_w` (generated; they test the code's values, and no value of the code changed)
- **Regression predictions:** wording; no value changes.
- **Validation:** fixture `bug0476.sales.market_discount_code_d` (the BUG-0476 witness, sales.box.D read as a tax-exempt bond bought at a market discount: code other, Schedule D line 16 and Form 1040 line 7a refused), predicted by hand before recording; every existing fixture passes.
- **Tags:** completeness; question-incomplete; refusal; fixed

## BUG-0485 — BUG-0477 is fixed: the capital loss carryover to 2026 is not shown on a decedent's final return

- **Date:** 2026-11-10
- **Closes:** BUG-0477
- **Caught by:** BUG-0477, recorded open; this entry closes it because the inventory is append-only.
- **Source:** p550 p. 103, Decedent's capital loss, "can be deducted only on the final income tax return filed for the decedent" and "The decedent's estate cannot deduct any of the loss or carry it over to following years".
- **Symptom:** as recorded in BUG-0477.
- **Fix:** asked; display only. `clcw26.final_return` asks whether this is the final return of a filer who died in 2025. It is gated (`clcw26.final_return_if_carryover`, through `clcw26.final_ask`, both of whose operands are figured lines): asked only when a carryover to 2026 is figured (`clcw26.show`) on a return other than a joint return (`clcw26.not_joint`, read from `f8880.joint` so that no new reader of the filing status moves the premises pinned for other forms' mutants); a joint return keeps `clcw26.decedent_notice`, since there only the deceased spouse's part of the carryover stops and the split between the spouses is not modeled (the screen review of `clcw26.final_ask` and the transcription review of lines 8 and 13 raised the joint case; ruled). On a final return lines 8 and 13 are not shown (their `shown_when` is now `clcw26.show_st_carry` / `clcw26.show_lt_carry`, which add `clcw26.carries`), and `clcw26.final_notice` says the loss does not carry to 2026 and the estate cannot deduct it. The lines' values are still figured; no other line reads them.
- **Fix lines:** `clcw26.line8`, `clcw26.line13`, `clcw26.final_return`
- **Siblings checked:** `clcw26.decedent_notice` (generated; the joint-return notice, unchanged), `clcw26.final_return_if_carryover` (generated; the input's gate line, new here)
- **Regression predictions:** no recorded value changes. The test-data default is No. 68 complete-return fixtures without defaults (class M and mutation cases, single, head of household, separate or surviving-spouse returns with a carryover figured) reach the new question and gain the answer `clcw26.final_return: false` (none is described as a final return); none of their asserted values changes.
- **Validation:** fixtures `bug0477.clcw26.final_return_long` (the BUG-0477 witness as a final return: line 13 figured at $2,000, not shown, notice given), `bug0477.clcw26.not_final_return`, `bug0477.clcw26.final_return_short` (line 8, $3,000, not shown) and `bug0477.clcw26.not_final_return_short`, each predicted by hand before recording; every existing fixture passes; interview-rules and mutation clean.
- **Tags:** completeness; question-incomplete; display; fixed

## BUG-0488 — Three sales rules are neither asked nor refused: a loss after extraordinary dividends, constructive ownership gain, and same-day wash-sale blocks

- **Date:** 2026-11-10
- **Caught by:** standing completeness review of `sales` (claims sales#1, sales#3 and sales#7 of prompt d51fbc85), adjudicated in the BUG-0474 to BUG-0478 review round; the claims' rulings in `reviews/2025/completeness/rulings.json` cite this entry.
- **Source:** i1040sd p. 4, "If qualified dividends that you reported on Form 1040, 1040-SR, or 1040-NR, line 3a, include extraordinary dividends, any loss on the sale or exchange of the stock is a long-term capital loss to the extent of the extraordinary dividends"; p550 p. 79, Gains From Certain Constructive Ownership Transactions, "all or part of the gain may be treated instead as ordinary income"; p550 p. 87, "Loss from a wash sale of one block of stock or securities cannot be used to reduce any gains on identical blocks sold the same day".
- **Symptom:** three rules the sales questions neither ask nor refuse. (1) A loss on stock held one year or less whose qualified dividends included an extraordinary dividend is classified short-term by `sales.box` (from the holding period), though it is long-term to the extent of the extraordinary dividends. (2) Gain from a constructive ownership transaction is computed as capital gain in full. (3) `sales.wash_loss` is capped at the loss of the row (`sales.wash_bad`), so blocks of identical stock sold the same day entered as one row let a gain block absorb the disallowed loss of another; the question does not say to enter each block separately.
- **Where:** `forms/2025/sales.yaml` (`sales.box`, `sales.special`, `sales.wash_loss`); `interview/questions-2025.yaml` (`$sales`).
- **Witness:** not executed; read from the questions' text (none of the three rules is named in `sales.box`, `sales.special`, `sales.code` or `sales.wash_loss`, nor in `sd.other_forms`).
- **Proposed disposition:** open, low. Name the extraordinary-dividend rule in the `sales.box` question, add constructive ownership transactions to `sales.special` (refused), and say in `sales.wash_loss` or `$sales` that blocks sold the same day are entered one row per block.
- **Tags:** completeness; question-incomplete; open

## BUG-0495 — siblings.py --check cannot find a fix entry renumbered at a merge, so the check fails on main

- **Date:** 2026-11-10
- **Caught by:** the BUG-0472 fix round, running `tools/siblings.py --check` on a tree branched from `b9c5b37d`.
- **Symptom:** `siblings.py --check` fails on `main` at `b9c5b37d` with "BUG-0492: no review log changed since HEAD for sibling form(s): dependent, eic, household, ny_it201, person, s1a, sd" and "BUG-0493: no review log changed since HEAD for sibling form(s): household, person, s1a", although their reviews were rerun on the branch. The two entries were renumbered from BUG-0482 and BUG-0483 in the merge commit `b9c5b37d`, so the heading "## BUG-0492 " first appears in that merge. `entry_base` finds the adding commit with `git log -1 -S "## BUG-0492 " -- BUG_INVENTORY.md`, which does not search merge commits; it finds nothing and falls back to HEAD, and against HEAD no review log has changed. Every fix entry renumbered at a merge fails the check in the same way, and only a review rerun in the next commit clears it. The `siblings_check` step of check-all fails for every tree branched from `b9c5b37d`. The last green full-tier run recorded in check-all-bg was on base `62c47c07`, before the merge.
- **Where:** `tools/siblings.py`, `entry_base` (the `git log -S` call). Possible fixes: `-m --first-parent`, so the search finds the merge and measures from its first parent; or measure a renumbered entry from the base the merge records.
- **Witness (executed):** `git log -1 --format=%H -S "## BUG-0492 " -- BUG_INVENTORY.md` prints nothing; with `-m` it prints `b9c5b37d`.
- **Disposition:** fixed. `entry_base` searches with `--first-parent --diff-merges=first-parent`, so an entry is attributed to the commit that brought it onto this line of history; BUG-0492 and BUG-0493 resolve to `b9c5b37d`, BUG-0482 to BUG-0486 to `62c47c07` (the old search had matched the branches' differently numbered entries of the same heading), older entries as before. The renumbered entries in the inventory are the regression case of `siblings.py --self-test` and `--check`. The cause was renumbering entries inside a merge commit; when merging, renumber in a commit of their own on the branch first.
- **Tags:** tooling; check-all; merge; fixed

- **Date:** 2026-11-10
- **Caught by:** siblings_check failing on main at 96ef8a7b, found while renaming the interview files.
- **Source:** `entry_base` (tools/siblings.py) found the commit that added an entry with `git log -S "## BUG-NNNN "`, which counts the string anywhere. BUG-0495's body quotes `-S "## BUG-0492 "`, so the commit that added BUG-0495 changed that count and the search attributed BUG-0492 to it, measuring its sibling refresh from the wrong base.
- **Symptom:** `siblings.py --check` failed on main from 96ef8a7b: "BUG-0492: no review log changed since 96ef8a7b^ for sibling form(s): dependent, household, ny_it201, s1a, sd".
- **Disposition:** fixed: the search matches the heading line, `-G "^## BUG-NNNN "` (with BUG-0495's `--first-parent --diff-merges=first-parent`). BUG-0492 resolves to b9c5b37d again; BUG-0482, BUG-0471, BUG-0494 and older entries as before. siblings.py --check and --self-test pass.
- **Tags:** tooling; check-all; siblings; fixed

## BUG-0498 — The Form 5695 window questions (lines 20a(i) to (iv)) admit windows that meet only the basic Energy Star requirements

- **Date:** 2026-11-10
- **Caught by:** question review pilot, f5695.line20a_i#1 (finding 1), 2026-11-10.
- **Source:** fs-2025-01, Energy Efficient Home Improvement Credit - Energy efficiency requirements, A1: "Exterior windows and skylights: must meet Energy Star most efficient certification requirements."; i5695 p. 6, Line 20b, "all other exterior windows and skylights that meet Energy Star most efficient certification requirements". (i5695 p. 6, Line 20a itself says only "meet Energy Star certification requirements".)
- **Symptom:** `f5695.line20a_i` to `f5695.line20a_iv` ask for the cost of a window or skylight "that meets the Energy Star certification requirements". A filer whose window carries the ordinary Energy Star label but not the Most Efficient designation enters its cost, which flows through line 20c into the 30% credit (up to the $600 window limit). `f5695.qmid_windows` asks only for the manufacturer's four-character QMID, which such a window can carry, so it does not screen the case.
- **Where:** `forms/2025/f5695.yaml`, `f5695.line20a_i`, `f5695.line20a_ii`, `f5695.line20a_iii`, `f5695.line20a_iv` (read by `f5695.line20c`).
- **Fix sketch:** ask for windows and skylights that meet the Energy Star Most Efficient certification requirements, citing fs-2025-01 A1 beside i5695 line 20a; line 20b already says so.
- **Status:** open
- **Tags:** question-incomplete; caught-by-question-review; open

## BUG-0499 — The code-screen question does not catch a code 2 exception that applies to none of the distribution

- **Date:** 2026-11-10
- **Caught by:** question review pilot, retirement.code_screen#1 (findings 0 to 2), 2026-11-10.
- **Source:** i5329 p. 1, Who Must File, "but box 7 of your Form 1099-R doesn't indicate an exception or the exception doesn't apply to the entire distribution"; i5329 p. 5, Line 2, exception 13, "Distributions from a section 457 plan, which aren't from a rollover from a qualified retirement plan."
- **Symptom:** `retirement.code_screen` asks whether "the exception that code 2 shows covers only part of it". When the code 2 exception applies to none of the distribution (for example, the payer coded separation from service at 55 but the filer left service in an earlier year), a literal reader answers No, and the tool treats the distribution as excepted: `retirement.early` is true only for codes 1 and S, so no additional 10% tax is computed (value-changing). Two lows on the same question: the clause "its code is wrong because you were under age 59½ when you received it (code 7)" treats age alone as proof that code 7 is wrong, so a correctly coded 7 distribution under 59½ (a governmental 457(b) distribution, exception 13) draws Yes and is refused; and the clause can be read either as "yes whenever I was under 59½" or "yes only if the code is wrong". Both lows only refuse (`retirement.screen_refused`).
- **Where:** `forms/2025/retirement.yaml`, `retirement.code_screen` (read by `retirement.screen_refused`).
- **Fix sketch:** ask whether the code 2 exception "does not apply to all of it" (covering none and part); reword the code 7 clause to ask whether code 7 is wrong (an early distribution with no exception), not whether the filer was under 59½.
- **Status:** open
- **Tags:** question-incomplete; caught-by-question-review; open

## BUG-0500 — The 80% meals question counts only the filer's own DOT duty periods, not employees'

- **Date:** 2026-11-10
- **Caught by:** question review pilot, sc.meals_80#1 (finding 0), 2026-11-10.
- **Source:** i1040sc p. 10, Line 24b, "for individuals subject to the Department of Transportation (DOT) hours of service limits, the percentage is increased to 80% for business meals consumed during or incident to any period of duty for which those limits are in effect".
- **Symptom:** `sc.meals_80` asks for meals consumed during a period of duty "for which you were subject to" the hours of service limits. A sole proprietor whose employee drivers are subject to the limits, and whose business reimburses their duty meals under an accountable plan (not as wages), leaves those meals out or enters them at 50%, so line 24b is understated. `sc.meals_50` also names only meals "while you travel away from home", so employees' reimbursed travel meals have no clear question at all; check this when fixing.
- **Where:** `forms/2025/sc.yaml`, `sc.meals_80` (read by `sc.meals_80_ded`, line 24b); `sc.meals_50` for the employee-travel gap.
- **Fix sketch:** ask for meals consumed by you or your employees during or incident to a period of duty under the DOT hours of service limits; say where employees' reimbursed travel meals go.
- **Status:** open
- **Tags:** question-incomplete; caught-by-question-review; open

## BUG-0501 — The New York 414(h) question asks only about the filer, not the spouse on a joint return

- **Date:** 2026-11-10
- **Caught by:** question review pilot, ny_it201.ask.414h#1 (findings 0 and 1), 2026-11-10.
- **Source:** IT-201-I p. 8, Line 21, "enter the amount of 414(h) retirement contributions, if shown on any federal Form W-2, Wage and tax statement if you are: – a member of the New York State and Local Retirement Systems ...".
- **Symptom:** `ny_it201.ask.414h` asks "Are you a public employee of New York State or its local governments with 414(h) retirement contributions shown on a Form W-2?". On a joint return where only the spouse is a member of a listed system, the filer answers No; `ny_it201.line21` is then zero (the tool computes no addition; Yes refuses through `ny_it201.gate.line21`), so New York AGI omits the addition (value-changing). A low on the same question: membership in one of the listed retirement systems appears only in the help, so a public employee who is not a member answers Yes and is refused (safe).
- **Where:** `forms/ny/2025/ny_it201.yaml`, `ny_it201.ask.414h` (read by `ny_it201.gate.line21`, the refusal on `ny_it201.line21`).
- **Fix sketch:** ask whether you or your spouse (on a joint return) is a member of one of the listed systems with 414(h) contributions on a Form W-2.
- **Status:** open
- **Tags:** question-incomplete; caught-by-question-review; ny; open

## BUG-0503 — Education credit question wording: fees required for attendance, an exclusion list given by reference, and 'at a college' in the gate (lows)

- **Date:** 2026-11-10
- **Caught by:** question review pilot, dependent.edu_inst#1 (finding 0), person.edu_mat#1 (finding 0), f8863.paid#1 (finding 0), 2026-11-10.
- **Source:** i8863 p. 4, Qualified Education Expenses, "tuition and fees required for the student's enrollment or attendance" and "nonacademic fees ... only if the fee must be paid to the institution as a condition of enrollment or attendance"; i8863 p. 2, Table 1, course materials "whether or not the materials are bought at the educational institution".
- **Symptom:** Three wording lows, recorded for the next change of these questions. (1) `dependent.edu_inst` and `person.edu_inst` list "required enrollment fees" without "or attendance" and do not say that mandatory nonacademic fees paid to the institution count; most filers would include a fee every enrolled student must pay. (2) `person.edu_mat` and `dependent.edu_mat` apply "the same exclusions as for the expenses paid to the institution" without restating them; the list is in the preceding question. (3) `f8863.paid` asks about expenses paid "at a college, university, vocational school or other postsecondary school (for tuition, required fees or course materials)", which can be read as paid to the school; the parenthetical names course materials, so few filers would answer No.
- **Where:** `forms/2025/dependent.yaml` and `forms/2025/person.yaml` (`edu_inst`, `edu_mat`); `forms/2025/f8863.yaml` (`f8863.paid`).
- **Fix sketch:** add "or attendance, including mandatory student activity, athletic or lab fees paid to the institution"; restate the exclusions in edu_mat; say "for a student at" in f8863.paid and that materials bought elsewhere count.
- **Status:** open
- **Tags:** wording; low; caught-by-question-review; open
