The Form 5471 instructions are not archived.
- **Symptom:** an unpaid board member, trustee, secretary or treasurer of a foreign charity, church, school, club or association that is incorporated abroad, with no shares and no foreign account, may not see that body as a corporation or company and answers No; `sb.form5471` is then not asked and its refusal is not made. The gated screen uses the form's own words ("officer or director of a foreign corporation") with the gate's roles and company forms, so the same filer would likely answer it No as well: the gate drops no refusal the screen alone would have made. Not reproduced; whether Form 5471 applies to a body without stock is not decided from an archived page.
- **Why the checks missed it:** the earlier false-no samples of the gate and the screen reviews of `sb.form5471` did not raise bodies that are incorporated but not businesses.
- **Disposition:** open, low: at the form's next substantive change, name incorporated nonprofits and associations in the gate's Form 5471 bullet and in `sb.form5471` (or archive the Form 5471 instructions and word both from them), and rerun the gate's false-no and screen reviews.
- **Tags:** schedule-b; gate; false-no; wording; low; open

## BUG-0595 — sb.line8 does not ask a filer treated as the owner of a foreign trust who is neither its grantor nor a transferor

- **Caught by:** the screen review of `sb.line8` (claude-fable-5-2), run twice in the U2 umbrella gate lane after the question's wording changed, 2026-11-10 (NARROW in both; ruled low in `reviews/2025/screens/rulings.json`, `unruled:sb.line8#1`).
- **Source:** `forms/2025/sb.yaml` `sb.line8` ("did you (or, on a joint return, your spouse) receive a distribution from a foreign trust ..., or were you (or, on a joint return, your spouse) the grantor of, or a transferor to, a foreign trust that existed at any time during 2025 ...") against i1040sb p. 3, Line 8 ("If you were treated as the owner of a foreign trust under the grantor trust rules, you are also responsible for ensuring that the foreign trust files Form 3520-A"). Schedule B line 8 as printed asks only "did you receive a distribution from, or were you the grantor of, or transferor to, a foreign trust".
- **Symptom:** a filer treated as the owner of a foreign trust under the grantor trust rules who neither created nor funded it (for example a beneficiary with a power to withdraw trust property) and who received no distribution, loan or use of trust property in 2025 can answer No truthfully; Schedule B lines 2, 3 and 6 are then computed without the refusal, although the Form 3520 and Form 3520-A duties the tool does not handle may apply. The foreign question before it (`sb.foreign_any`) counts "being a beneficiary of a foreign trust", so this filer reaches the screen. Not reproduced; rare.
- **Why the checks missed it:** earlier screen reviews of `sb.line8` did not raise the owner sentence; the question follows the printed line.
- **Disposition:** open, low: not fixed in the wording (owner decision, 2026-11-10: the question follows the printed line 8). If it is taken up, archive the Form 3520 and Form 3520-A instructions first, then decide whether a separate owner question refuses.
- **Tags:** schedule-b; screen; foreign-trust; wording; low; open

## BUG-0596 — Spouse wording on Form 5695, Schedule 1-A, Form 2441 and New York IT-201 reads correctly for single and joint filers (source-check fixes)

- **Date:** 2026-11-11
- **Caught by:** an independent source check of the spouse wording merged from four question-fix lanes (38 edited questions on Form 5695, Schedule 1-A, Form 2441, dividends and New York IT-201). None was wrong; eight were awkward and four carried a second spouse wording. A reading of all 81 spouse-phrased questions with the phrase removed and with it replaced added six more (Schedule 1, the student loan interest worksheet, the social security benefits worksheet and the household questions).
- **Source:** i5695 p. 2, Joint occupancy, "These rules don't apply to married individuals filing a joint return."; i5695 p. 1, Purpose of Form, "Also use Form 5695 to take any residential clean energy credit carryforward from 2024"; i1040gi p. 13, Married Filing Jointly, "A married couple filing jointly report their combined income and deduct their combined allowable expenses on one return."; i1040gi pp. 101, 106 and 109 (Schedule 1-A, Parts II to IV); i2441 p. 1, Purpose of Form, and p. 5, Lines 13 and 14; IT-201-I p. 5, Item G, and p. 31, Special accruals; IT-225-I p. 8, A-103; IT-112-R-I p. 2, Column A.
- **Symptom:** stored spouse wording must be exactly "(or, on a joint return, your spouse)" or "your (or, on a joint return, your spouse's)" (interview/README.md, Question data), must read correctly for a filer who is not filing jointly, and must not leave a joint filer answering for themselves only. Against that: `f5695.part1_any` named the spouse for the costs clause only ("or do you have a ... carryforward"), so a joint filer whose spouse alone has a 2024 carryforward could answer No, and `f5695.line12` asked for "your 2024 Form 5695" only; `s1a.tips`, `s1a.overtime` and `s1a.carloan` added "Answer Yes if either of you did.", which a single filer also reads; `f2441.line13` and `f2441.line14` carried the phrase twice with a bare "you" for what may be the spouse's amount, and did not say that two spouses' amounts are totalled; `ny_it201.ask.special_accrual` carried the phrase twice with "that person", and `ny_it201.ask.special_code` had two parentheses back to back; `f2441.care` ("or your spouse, if filing jointly") and `f2441.nondependent` ("or your spouse") kept an older phrasing beside the new one; the help of `ny_it201.ask.414h` began a sentence with spouse wording of its own.
- **Root cause:** the lanes added the phrase clause by clause and did not read each edited question once with the phrase removed (the single filer's reading) and once with it replaced by "or your spouse" (the joint filer's reading).
- **Where:** `forms/2025/f5695.yaml`, `forms/2025/s1a.yaml`, `forms/2025/f2441.yaml`, `forms/ny/2025/ny_it201.yaml`, `forms/2025/s1.yaml`, `forms/2025/sli.yaml`, `forms/2025/ssb.yaml`, `forms/2025/household.yaml`, `interview/2025/questions.yaml`, `interview/ny/2025/questions.yaml`, `engine/src/mutate.ts`.
- **Fix:**
  - `f5695.part1_any`: "Did you (or, on a joint return, your spouse) have 2025 costs for ... for a home in the United States, or a residential clean energy credit carryforward from line 16 of a 2024 Form 5695?", so the one phrase governs both clauses.
  - `f5695.part1_any` help: "Answer Yes also if the only Part I amount is a carryforward from 2024." (it said "your only Part I amount").
  - `f5695.line12`: "... the amount on line 16 of your (or, on a joint return, your spouse's) 2024 Form 5695, or the total of those amounts if there is more than one such form (zero if none)" (owner decision: a spouse's own 2024 carryforward is counted on the joint return; see the next entry). Line 12 is an amount read only by line 13, a sum, so a total of two carryforwards needs no other change.
  - `s1a.tips`, `s1a.overtime`, `s1a.carloan`: the sentence "Answer Yes if either of you did." is removed; nothing else changes.
  - `f2441.line13`: "The amount, if any, carried forward from 2024 under a dependent care plan of your (or, on a joint return, your spouse's) employer and used in 2025 during the plan's grace period; the total if there is more than one such plan; zero if none".
  - `f2441.line14`: "Of the dependent care benefits on line 12, the total of the amounts you (or, on a joint return, your spouse) forfeited (did not receive because the expense was not incurred) and the amounts not received that an employer permits to be carried forward and used in 2026; do not include amounts expected to be received later; zero if none".
  - `f2441.care` and `f2441.nondependent`: the older phrasings are replaced by the one phrase; "so that you (and your spouse) could work or look for work" stays, since "and" is its meaning.
  - `ny_it201.ask.special_accrual`: "Does this apply to you (or, on a joint return, your spouse): the person was a New York City nonresident on December 31, 2024, or will be a New York State or City nonresident on January 1, 2026, and has income fixed and determinable in one tax year but reported federally in another (accrued income)?"
  - `ny_it201.ask.special_code`: "Does any New York special condition code (item G) apply to you (or, on a joint return, your spouse)? Examples: A6 Build America Bond interest, ..."
  - `ny_it201.ask.414h` help: the spouse sentence is removed; the question already names the spouse.
  - `s1.cod_amount`: the clause "count a debt you both owed once, even if each of you received a Form 1099-C for the whole amount" becomes a conditional sentence true for every filer, "On a joint return, count a debt both spouses owed once, even if each received a Form 1099-C for the whole amount" (p4681 p. 4).
  - `s1.cod_unsupported`: the last item reads "you (or, on a joint return, your spouse) were liable for it together with someone who is not on this return" (label: "a debt owed jointly with someone who is not on this return"), which names no spouse to a filer who has none.
  - `s1.alimony` help: "On a joint return, payments between the two spouses are not alimony."
  - `sli.interest`: the older "(or your spouse if filing jointly)" in the eligible-student list is the one phrase (i1040gi p. 99, "You, or your spouse if filing jointly, could be claimed as a dependent on someone else's return").
  - `ssb.pub915`: "and you (or, on a joint return, your spouse) were covered by a retirement plan" (i1040gi p. 31, "you or your spouse were covered by a retirement plan at work or through self-employment").
  - `household.credit_disallowed`: "Was your (or, on a joint return, your spouse's) earned income credit for any year after 1996, or child tax credit, additional child tax credit or credit for other dependents for any year after 2015, reduced or disallowed ..., or are you (or, on a joint return, your spouse) in a 2- or 10-year period during which one of these credits can't be taken ..."; the label likewise; the help no longer says "either of you". The question is asked whenever the return claims one of these credits (`household.credit_disallowed_if_claimed`), on joint returns too, so the phrase belongs.
  - Citations: the i5695 p. 2 joint-return sentence is added to `f5695.line1` to `line4`, `line5a` and `battery_cost`; i1040gi p. 13 to `f5695.line12`; IT-225-I p. 8, A-103, to `ny_it201.ask.529_nonqualified`; IT-112-R-I p. 2, Column A, to `ny_it201.ask.resident_credit`.
  - The 17 pinned mutation arguments whose premises include `s1a.tips`, `s1a.overtime` or `s1a.carloan` are re-pinned: with the three questions put back to their earlier wording the tool's `premiseDigest` gives each pinned digest, so wording is the only difference; only the digest strings change.
- **Regression predictions:** wording and citations only; no recorded value changes.
- **Validation:** a mechanical check on the parsed values: every spouse wording added or changed is one of the two phrases, in lower case, after "you" or "your" and not sentence-initial, and each edited question was read with the phrase removed and with it replaced by "or your spouse" or "or your spouse's". Every federal and New York fixture passes; the reviews made due by the wording changes (transcription and render lines of f5695, s1a, f2441 and ny_it201; transcription of dependent and s3, which read the reworded questions; transcription and render lines of s1, sli, ssb and household) are rerun and ruled.
- **Tags:** wording; spouse-phrase; fixed

## BUG-0597 — A spouse's own 2024 residential clean energy credit carryforward is counted on a joint return on the general joint-return rule; the Form 5695 instructions are silent

- **Caught by:** source check of the spouse wording on `f5695.part1_any`, 2026-11-11.
- **Symptom:** `f5695.part1_any` and `f5695.line12` count, on a joint 2025 return, a residential clean energy credit carryforward that the spouse brings from a 2024 Form 5695 of their own (a couple who married in 2025, or who filed separately for 2024), and line 12 takes the total when each spouse has one. The Form 5695 instructions do not address this case: they speak only of "any residential clean energy credit carryforward from 2024" and of "your 2024 Form 5695, line 16". The model's reading rests on the general joint-return rule alone (owner decision, 2026-11-11). If the reading were wrong, line 12 and with it the credit on line 15 and Schedule 3 line 5a would be overstated by the spouse's carryforward on such a return.
- **Source:** i5695 p. 1, Purpose of Form, "Also use Form 5695 to take any residential clean energy credit carryforward from 2024 or to carry the unused portion of the residential clean energy credit to 2026."; f5695 (2025), line 12; i1040gi p. 13, Married Filing Jointly, "A married couple filing jointly report their combined income and deduct their combined allowable expenses on one return."; i5695 p. 2, Joint occupancy, "These rules don't apply to married individuals filing a joint return."
- **Severity:** low (rare: a carryforward on each of two separate 2024 returns, or on the 2024 return of a spouse married in 2025; amount-affecting when it occurs).
- **Status:** open

## BUG-0598 — The Lean comparison's generated returns computed no return's tax: three quarters of their compared values were unknowns

- **Date:** 2026-11-11
- **Caught by:** T-259, measuring the old corpus before replacing it (scratch scripts `/tmp/qfix/t259/analyze.mjs`, `old_kinds.mjs`, run on main at `bf599378`).
- **Symptom:** `compare` reported agreement on 1,557,802 line values from 600 generated cases, but 1,172,786 of them (75%) were unknowns, which the comparison checks by kind only. On all 600 cases Form 1040 line 24 was unknown (497) or a refusal (103): no generated case reached a computed total tax. The hand-written generator in `engine/src/compare.ts` gave 66 of the 564 federal input lines and varied 15; every input added to the model after it was written was absent, so lines that read them were unknown. `compare --ny` used the same federal cases, with no New York answer in any of them.
- **Where:** `engine/src/compare.ts`, `generatedCases` (its own generator and input list); `reports/2025/evaluator_agreement.md` and `reports/ny/2025/evaluator_agreement.md`, whose single count did not show how many values were unknowns.
- **Witness (executed):** `node /tmp/qfix/t259/old_kinds.mjs` on the old generator: `{"cases":600,"total":1557802,"kinds":{"money":211859,"unknown":1172786,"bool":87218,"enum":2814,"rate":6000,"count":13572,"refusal":63553}}`; `analyze.mjs . old`: `fedGiven 66, fedVaried 15, line24 {unknown 497, refusal 103}`.
- **Disposition:** fixed (T-259). The generated cases are the general generator's (`generate.ts` `sampleReturns`; `nyReturnArbitrary` for `--ny`), seed 7, 400 returns, the corpus of the properties check: 562 of 564 federal input lines given and 423 varied (all 43 New York input lines varied with `--ny`); 110 returns compute line 24 and 290 are refused; 1,247,601 federal line values compared, 74,204 of them unknowns. The report now counts compared values by kind and what was not compared by reason, and the self-test plants 16 differences on generated returns, one or more per value kind on computed lines. No disagreement between the evaluators was found on the new corpus. The fixture cases were and are compared in full; the claim was weak only for generated returns.
- **Tags:** verification; lean; compare; corpus; fixed

## BUG-0599 — A review run after npm run build reads rendered English from before the edit, and its log looks current

- **Date:** 2026-11-11
- **Caught by:** the question-wording fix lanes, 2026-11-10 and 2026-11-11: three agents edited question wording, ran `npm run build`, and ran paid render reviews that read `rendered/` files from before their edits; each paid for a second call, and one reported its render reviews current when they were current only against the old text.
- **Symptom:** `npm run build` writes `canonical/` and not the tracked `rendered/` files (`node engine/dist/main.js render` and check-all write those). A render log's subject is the hash of `rendered/<year>/<form>.md`, and the render request is built from the same files, so after an edit and a build without a render `rerun_all.py` reported "its log already answers the current subject" and planned no call, `check_logs.py` passed, and a forced or direct `render_compare.py` run sent the old English and recorded the old subject. Reproduced without a paid call in the process lane (a scratch label edit on `gift`; after the render the same tools reported three stale lines and a $0.13 line-scoped job). The screen, false-no and question reviews quote each line's rendered English in their prompts and subjects and had the same exposure.
- **Why the checks missed it:** `tools/build_fresh.py` compared `canonical/` and `engine/dist` with their sources and did not look at `rendered/`; check-all renders before its log checks, so a full run never saw the stale state, only the tools run by hand between an edit and the next check-all.
- **Disposition:** fixed. `node engine/dist/main.js render --check` compares `rendered/` with what the canonical data renders to, in memory, writing nothing; `build_fresh.require(rendered=True)` refuses on a stale build or a differing rendered file, naming the files and the command, and is called by `render_compare.py`, `rerun_all.py` (render jobs, `--dry-run` included), `check_logs.py`, `screen_review.py`, `false_no_review.py`, `question_review.py`, `check_screens.py`, `check_false_no.py` and `check_questions.py`.
- **Validation:** `build_fresh.py --self-test` renders into a temporary directory, plants an edited, a missing and a left-over file and checks that each is named with the regenerating command; `test_rerun_all.py` and `test_review_tools.py` check that the planner and the render review refuse before any request is built. No review subject changes and no log becomes stale: on a fresh rendering the planner's and `check_logs.py`'s output is identical to before the change.
- **Tags:** tool change; review process; cost; fixed

## BUG-0600 — Form 8863 Part III's two copies had drifted in four places; a check now keeps them in step

- **Date:** 2026-11-11
- **Caught by:** a study of the Form 8863 Part III block, which is written twice (`person.edu*` in `forms/2025/person.yaml` and `dependent.edu*` in `forms/2025/dependent.yaml`): the 38 paired lines were compared field by field after normalizing the document prefix.
- **Source:** i8863 p. 8, Line 23, Line 24, Line 25 and Line 26, and p. 9, Line 27 (the instruction sections of the five lines); i8863 p. 3, Who cannot claim a credit, "5. The student has not been issued a TIN by the due date of his or her 2025 return (including extensions)."; p970 p. 11, "You weren’t issued an SSN (or ITIN) by the due date of your 2025 return (including extensions)." and "a student who wasn’t issued an SSN, ATIN, or ITIN by the due date of your return (including extensions)"; i1040gi p. 20, Adoption taxpayer identification numbers (ATINs), "If you have a dependent who was placed with you for legal adoption and you don’t know the dependent’s SSN, you must get an ATIN for the dependent from the IRS."
- **Symptom:** four places where one copy had been changed and the other had not, none changing a value. (1) `dependent.edu_line23` to `dependent.edu_line27` cited their instruction sections ("; i8863 p. 8, Line 23" to "; i8863 p. 9, Line 27") and their person twins did not; the gap was accepted in the baseline of `reviews/2025/instruction_cites.json` (five entries), so reviews of the person's lines were not handed i8863 pp. 8-9 through those citations. (2) The operand finding on line 28 ("Subtract $2,000 from line 27"; not an operand: 27) had a reasoned ruling for `dependent.edu_line28` and only a baseline entry for `person.edu_line28` in `reviews/2025/operands.json`. (3) The label of `dependent.edu_student_tin` said "a TIN by the due date" although `dependent.tin` also counts an ITIN or ATIN only applied for; the person twin's label had been made exact. (4) `person.edu_line31` refused with "Lifetime learning credit for a student whose ITIN or ATIN was only applied for" (and the same words in the remedy), the dependent's text, although a person on the return cannot have an ATIN and the gate's own label (`person.edu_llc_tin_refused`) says ITIN.
- **Root cause:** the data model cannot state a block once for a person and for a dependent, so Part III exists twice, and nothing compared the copies: `tools/siblings.py` only required a bug entry to list the twin of a fixed line.
- **Where:** `forms/2025/person.yaml`, `forms/2025/dependent.yaml`, `reviews/2025/instruction_cites.json`, `reviews/2025/operands.json`, `fixtures/2025/person.json`; new `tools/check_twins.py` and `reviews/2025/twins.json`; `tools/siblings.py`, `tools/check_all_steps.sh`, `tools/self_tests.py`.
- **Fix:** (1) the locators of `person.edu_line23` to `person.edu_line27` end with the same instruction-section references as the dependent side, and the five baseline entries are removed (the check no longer reports them). (2) `operands:person.edu_line28` has the ruling of its twin (the line is bound to the `aqee` definition's line 28, whose operand is that definition's line 27) and its baseline entry is removed. (3) `dependent.edu_student_tin` is labelled "A student with qualified expenses: an SSN, ITIN or ATIN (or an ITIN or ATIN applied for by the due date), and a Form 1098-T (or an exception)". (4) `person.edu_line31` refuses with "Lifetime learning credit for a student whose ITIN was only applied for" and its remedy says "an ITIN only applied for by then"; the dependent side keeps "ITIN or ATIN", and the difference is declared with its source. The check: `tools/check_twins.py` (check-all step `twins`) pairs the two blocks by local id and the Form 8863 lines that sum them, compares every field of each pair, of its question bank entry and of its test-data default, and fails on any difference or one-sided id not declared with a reason and source in `reviews/2025/twins.json` (14 declared differences, 15 one-sided ids), and on a declaration that no longer matches the data. `tools/siblings.py` takes the pairing from the same file. `check_twins.py --sync-from SIDE [--write]` copies a field from one side to the other.
- **Fix lines:** `person.edu_line23`, `person.edu_line24`, `person.edu_line25`, `person.edu_line26`, `person.edu_line27`, `person.edu_line31`, `dependent.edu_student_tin`
- **Siblings checked:** `dependent.edu_line23`, `dependent.edu_line24`, `dependent.edu_line25`, `dependent.edu_line26`, `dependent.edu_line27` (the twins: already cite the sections; now equal), `dependent.edu_line31` (the twin: "ITIN or ATIN" is right for a dependent; declared difference), `person.edu_student_tin` (the twin: label already exact; declared difference), `person.edu_show24`, `person.edu_show25`, `person.edu_show26`, `person.edu_aoc23`, `person.edu_aoc24`, `person.edu_aoc25`, `person.edu_aoc26`, `person.edu_line28`, `person.edu_line29`, `person.edu_line30` (computed readers; equal to their twins, no change), `dependent.claimed_no_tin`, `dependent.ctc_from_tin`, `dependent.odc_person` (readers of `dependent.tin` outside Part III; no change), `person.edu_line27`, `person.edu_line31` (fix lines that are also siblings of the other fix lines; fixed here)
- **Regression predictions:** no value changes. The refusal text expected by `f1.t113.person_llc_itin_applied` (on `person[taxpayer].edu_line31` and `f8863.line10`) changes with the wording.
- **Validation:** every federal and New York fixture passes; the person transcription and render reviews of line 31 and the dependent render review of lines 27 to 31, made due by the wording changes, are rerun and ruled; `check_twins.py` fails on a changed operand, a reworded question, a changed citation and a new line planted on one side of the real forms, and passes on the forms as fixed.
- **Tags:** twin-drift; citation; wording; record-drift; tool change; fixed

## BUG-0601 — Form 8962's zero-column-(b) refusal test reads a monthly Form 1095-A's columns A and B before household income decides whether they are used

- **Date:** 2026-11-11
- **Caught by:** interview-rules on a scratch copy in which one unrelated input id was renamed (`eic.died_2025`), which changed the generated returns (`derivedStream` in `engine/src/generate.ts` hashes the input ids): 27 problems on `generated.0`. Reproduced on unmodified data (main at ddb6bd99) with a hand-built return, by a walk in bank order with the tool's own `walk`, `bankOrder` and `minimalAnswers`.
- **Source:** the BUG-0466 pattern, left in `f8962.b_zero`: `all(f8962.show_applicable, any(all(line 12a > 0, line 12b = 0), ..., all(line 23a > 0, line 23b = 0)))`. `f8962.show_applicable` is unknown until line 5 (household income as a percentage of the poverty line) is known, which the income questions decide later in bank order; the evaluator goes on past an unknown operand of `all`, so each month's column A, and column B while column A is unanswered or above zero, is reachable. `f8962.b_zero` is read by the refusal gate `f8962.two_counted` on `f8962.line24`. The same form's month figures (`f8962.line12e` and the like) are behind a `choose` on `f8962.applicable` and do not leak. i8962, Lines 12 Through 23, "skip columns (a) through (e), and complete only column (f)" (stated there for married filing separately; page number not checked; the model computes line 24 as zero for every taxpayer who is not applicable, `amb.2025.ptc_not_applicable`).
- **Symptom:** for a filer who is not an applicable taxpayer (line 5 below 100 and no Marketplace estimate exception), with one Form 1095-A entered month by month (`f1095a.uniform` No): the interview asks the 12 column A amounts, and column B for each month whose column A is above zero, and the completed return reads none of them. Witness (every other answer the minimal return's closed answer): coverage in December only, column A $1,245.69, column B $615.14, column C $472.84, `f8962.estimate_100` No. The interview asks 112 questions; 13 are unread (`f1095a.in_a_jan` to `in_a_dec`, `f1095a.in_b_dec`); `f1095a.in_b_jan` to `in_b_nov` are reachable until that month's column A is answered zero and are never asked in bank order (interview-rules: "is reachable before the answer that hides it, and the walk in bank order never asks it"). With all 12 months covered and no advance payments, 24 of 121 questions are unread. The uniform route shows the same on `f1095a.mo_a` and `f1095a.mo_b` (generated return 9 of seed 1). No value is affected: line 24 is zero and line 29 repays column C either way; the cost is up to 24 questions per form.
- **Where:** `forms/2025/f8962.yaml` (`f8962.b_zero`; read by `f8962.two_counted`), `forms/2025/f1095a.yaml` (`f1095a.in_a_*`, `f1095a.in_b_*`, `f1095a.mo_a`, `f1095a.mo_b`).
- **Severity:** low (questions only; no value changes).
- **Status:** open. Tried in memory only, not in the data: with `f8962.b_zero` as a `choose` on `f8962.show_applicable` (No: false; Yes: the month tests), the witness asks 99 questions, none unread and no column B out of order; fixtures, reviews and the month lines' `shown_when` (`f8962.show_jan` to `show_dec` read columns A and B, and are unknown at completion on the witness before and after) were not checked. BUG-0487 holds the same form's `f1095a.c_total`, `f8962.estimate_100` and `f8962.alien_below`; on the witness with no advance payments `f8962.estimate_100` is also reachable out of bank order, which no baseline list holds.
- **Tags:** interview; leak; conjunction; order-dependence; sample-dependent; open

## BUG-0602 — interview-rules classes only three generated returns, and its empty baseline holds for that sample alone

- **Date:** 2026-11-11
- **Caught by:** the same investigation: `INTERVIEW_RULES_RUNS=200 node engine/dist/main.js interview-rules` on unmodified data (main at ddb6bd99), and a scratch sweep of 20 fast-check seeds with 50 federal returns each, through the tool's own `runTask`.
- **Source:** `engine/src/interview-rules.ts`: `GENERATED` is 12 and `SEED` is the constant 11. Of the 12 federal generated returns 9 end refused and of the 12 New York ones all 12, and a refused return is not classed for reach or early completion, so 3 generated returns carry those rules. The minimal returns open Bool and enum gates only, never a collection roster (no Form 1095-A, dependent, Form 1099-R, HSA or vehicle entry). `derivedStream` in `engine/src/generate.ts` hashes the input ids with their values, so a renamed or added input redraws the answers taken from that stream (education, early distributions, Forms 1095-A and 8962; by the code also the carryover figures) on every generated return (BUG-0487 was caught the same way).
- **Symptom:** the check reports 0 problems on main, and with the same seed and 200 returns per profile reports 23: 6 templates left reachable at completion in a random order (`dependent.canada_mexico`, `gross_income`, `kidnapped`, `multiple_support`, `qr_all_year`, `supported`), 11 reached only out of bank order (`dependent.absence_no_return`, `edu_tin_issued`, `months`, `parent_home_paid`, `supported`; `f8889.employer_in_box1`; `person.died_before_65`, `person.tin`; `retirement.exception`; `scveh.owned`; `ssb.lived_apart`) and 6 asked and unread (`asset.not179`; `dependent.citizen`, `gross_income`, `lawful`, `supported`; `person.tin`). Over 20 other seeds: 14 of 20 show a problem in their first 12 returns, 20 of 20 in 50; 32 templates on nine forms over 1,000 returns (asset, dependent, f1095a, f5695, f8889, person, retirement, scveh, ssb), on 130 of the 201 complete returns. These are instances of BUG-0466 and BUG-0454 that the default sample does not draw; BUG-0492 records the baseline as empty.
- **Where:** `engine/src/interview-rules.ts` (`GENERATED`, `SEED`, the refused returns, the minimal returns), `engine/src/generate.ts` (`derivedStream`).
- **Severity:** medium for the check (a pass says little about returns it does not draw); low for each template found (questions only, by BUG-0466's reading; the early completions leave an input reachable with every target known).
- **Status:** open
- **Tags:** interview-rules; check-weakness; sampling; sample-dependent; open

## BUG-0603 — BUG-0602 in part: the credit-for-other-dependents and qualifying-relative tests read later operands past an undecided one; in some answer orders the interview reported complete with a question open whose answer refuses the return

- **Date:** 2026-11-11
- **Caught by:** the interview-rules catalog (T-276, BUG-0602): the tool's own rules over 5,000 generated federal returns, each cause traced on a witness return; reproduced before the fix on 2,000 generated returns (40 seeds of 50, 449 complete) at main's tip.
- **Source:** the BUG-0466 pattern in two lines of `forms/2025/dependent.yaml`. `dependent.odc_person` was `all(dependent.claimed, dependent.tin, dependent.citizen, dependent.ctc_child = false, household.all_tin)` and `dependent.qualifying_relative` was `all(dependent.qr_relationship, dependent.qualifying_child = false, dependent.qr_income, dependent.supported)`. An `all` goes on past an unknown operand and a later false operand decides it (spec 4.7.2), so a later operand's question is reachable, and can decide the line, before the earlier operand is known. i1040gi p. 18, Step 3, and p. 19, Steps 4 and 5.
- **Symptom:** (1) The serious one. With the dependent's SSN question, the citizenship question or the filer's own SSN or ITIN answered No before the dependent test was finished, `dependent.odc_person` was false while `dependent.claimed` was still unknown, every target was known, and the interview reported the return complete with questions of the dependent test still open. An answer to some of those open questions refuses the return: `dependent.multiple_support` and `dependent.kidnapped` (through `dependent.qr_kidnapped`) at every such state probed, and `dependent.canada_mexico`, `dependent.disabled` and `dependent.gross_income` at some (gates `dependent.claimed_no_tin` and `dependent.income_exception`). On the 2,000 returns: 96 states on 47 returns reported complete with a question open, and at 37 of the open questions an answer refused the return. No answer changed a value while the return stayed complete, and the bank order asks the dependent test first, so a walk in bank order did not meet it; another order of answers, or a corrected earlier answer, could. (2) Questions asked for nothing: `dependent.citizen` was asked and unread on 83 of the 449 complete returns, `dependent.supported` on 22, `dependent.gross_income` on 25, `person.tin` on 7 and `person.itin_applied` on 1; `dependent.supported` and `person.tin` were also reachable out of bank order (37 and 31 returns).
- **Where:** `forms/2025/dependent.yaml` (`dependent.odc_person`, `dependent.qualifying_relative`).
- **Severity:** medium (an interview could report complete with a question open whose answer refuses the return; no value of a complete return was wrong).
- **Fix:** `dependent.qualifying_relative` must not be rewritten without `dependent.odc_person`: alone it makes the interview ask `person.tin` for nothing on 3 of 449 complete returns, through the old `all` of `dependent.odc_person`. Each line is a nested `choose` on its operands in their original order, with the false alternative `dependent.no` (the BUG-0471 convention), so an operand is read only once the ones before it are known and pass. `dependent.odc_person` chooses on `dependent.claimed`, then `dependent.odc_from_tin` (the person's SSN, ITIN or ATIN), `dependent.odc_from_citizen` (citizenship) and `dependent.odc_from_ctc` (not a qualifying child for the child tax credit, then `household.all_tin`). `dependent.qualifying_relative` chooses on `dependent.qr_relationship`, then `dependent.qr_from_child` (not a qualifying child) and `dependent.qr_from_income` (the gross income test, then `dependent.supported`); its four refusal gates are unchanged. The five helper lines are at the end of the document's lines, each with the citation of the line it serves. Labels and question text of existing lines are unchanged.
- **Fix lines:** `dependent.odc_person`, `dependent.qualifying_relative`
- **Siblings checked:** `dependent.odc_amount`, `s8812.line6` (the readers of `dependent.odc_person`; its value on every complete return is unchanged, no change), `dependent.eic_child`, `dependent.hoh_test2_lived`, `dependent.qualifying_child` (the lines the sibling tool gives for `dependent.qualifying_relative`; no expression change). The other conjunctions of the same shape on this form (`dependent.income_exception`, `dependent.qr_other_relation`, `dependent.qr_household_member`, `dependent.hoh_test1`, `dependent.hoh_test2`, `dependent.hoh_test2_lived`, `dependent.edu_llc_tin_refused`) are left as they are (T-276, the owner's decision); with this fix `dependent.gross_income` is reachable out of bank order through `dependent.income_exception` on more returns than before (38 of 449 against 13), where it was asked and unread before
- **Regression predictions:** no complete return's value or refusal changes. On incomplete states a value the three-valued `all` decided from a later operand is unknown until the earlier operand is known (the trade-off the owner accepted in BUG-0471): on the evaluator's own truth tables over true, false, unknown, gate-pending and refused operands (3,125 combinations for `dependent.odc_person`, 625 for `dependent.qualifying_relative`), the old and new line agree wherever every operand is known, every difference has an unknown operand before the deciding one, and the new value is then unknown where the old was false or a later operand's refusal. No asserted fixture holds such a state.
- **Validation:** Each family alone and the four of this round together (BUG-0603, BUG-0604): every federal and New York fixture passes with no expected value, refusal or completion changed (the class M cases of dependent and f8962 were regenerated by this round's class M reviews); status and every target value are identical to main on 3,000 generated returns (712 complete; 1,500 for each family alone) and on every fixture's inputs. Evaluator truth tables as stated under Regression predictions. Sweep of 2,000 generated returns (40 seeds of 50; 449 complete), return by return against main: status differs on none and no order error; with the four families 342 fewer questions on complete returns (130 returns shorter, none longer; `dependent.odc_person` alone 94 on 84 returns, `dependent.qualifying_relative` alone 44) and no refused return longer; asked-and-unread questions 373 to 31; every template this entry names is gone. The states that reported complete with a question open fall from 96 (37 open questions with a refusing answer) to 24, at none of which any answer refuses the return or changes a value. One early completion appears that the base sweep did not show, `dependent.absence_no_return` on one return, through the lower bound of a count (`household.any_test2_person`), the class BUG-0602 leaves to the owner. `interview-rules` reports 0 problems, and with 200 generated returns 12 where main reports 23, none an early completion. Mutation: no survivor unexplained. Six pinned arguments whose premises changed were re-read against the new expressions and hold as written (`f8962.filing` reading `f8962.show_applicable`; the false alternatives of `dependent.qr_dependent`, `dependent.qr_kidnapped` and `dependent.eic_ssn_child`; the married gate of `dependent.qualifying_relative`; `dependent.dc_line2c`), and five new survivors on the new lines have pinned arguments (the false alternatives of `dependent.qualifying_relative`, `dependent.odc_person`, `dependent.odc_from_tin`, `f8962.alien_branch` and `f8962.estimate_exception`); each of the eleven was also compared with the unmutated data on 3,000 generated returns with answers withheld at six rates, every line but the mutated one, with no difference beyond the one the argument on the married gate already names. Reviews (claude-fable-5-2; $14.13 in 17 ledger rows for this entry and BUG-0604 together): transcription (whole), render and class M of dependent, and a line-scoped transcription of Schedule 8812 line 6 as the sibling refresh (agrees). Render: 6 lines match. Class M: 12 lines agree. Transcription: 20 disagreements, all ruled, none a finding; on `dependent.odc_person` the reply has the project's operands and no value differs on a completed return, and the differences are the reply's dependency screens read for every entry and a filer who can be claimed as a dependent on a joint return (refused: scope). Made due and not run, as sampled reviews: the screens `dependent.married` and `dependent.multiple_support` (next release) and the questions `dependent.citizen` and `dependent.supported` (next full pass).
- **Tags:** interview; leak; conjunction; order-dependence; early-completion; fixed

## BUG-0604 — BUG-0487 and BUG-0601 fixed: the Form 8962 applicable-taxpayer, lawfully-present-alien and zero-column-(b) tests are nested choose in their operands' order

- **Date:** 2026-11-11
- **Caught by:** BUG-0487 (held in the interview-rules baseline) and BUG-0601, recorded open; this entry records their fix because the inventory is append-only. Reproduced before the fix on 2,000 generated returns (40 seeds of 50, 449 complete) at main's tip and on the three hand-built returns of BUG-0601.
- **Source:** as recorded in BUG-0487 and BUG-0601: the BUG-0466 pattern in three lines of `forms/2025/f8962.yaml`. `f8962.applicable` was `any(line 5 at least 100, all(f8962.aptc, f8962.estimate_100))`, `f8962.alien_branch` was `all(f8962.any, line 5 below 100, f8962.alien_below)` and `f8962.b_zero` was `all(f8962.show_applicable, <a month with column (a) above zero and column (b) zero>)`; line 5 (household income as a percentage of the poverty line) is known only once the income questions later in bank order are answered. i8962 p. 6, Applicable taxpayer; p. 9, Line 5; p. 16, Column (b).
- **Symptom:** as recorded in BUG-0487 and BUG-0601. On the 449 complete returns: `f8962.estimate_100` and `f8962.alien_below` were asked and unread on 51 returns each and `f1095a.c_total` on 1; for filers who are not applicable taxpayers the monthly Form 1095-A columns A and B (`f1095a.in_a_*`, `f1095a.in_b_*`, or `f1095a.mo_a`, `f1095a.mo_b` and `f1095a.b_counted`) were asked and unread, and column B of a month was reachable out of bank order. No value was affected; the cost was questions (up to 24 amounts per Form 1095-A).
- **Where:** `forms/2025/f8962.yaml` (`f8962.applicable`, `f8962.alien_branch`, `f8962.b_zero`); `tools/interview_rules_baseline.json`.
- **Fix:** each line is a nested `choose` on its operands in their original order (the BUG-0471 convention), with `f8962.no` as the false alternative. `f8962.applicable` chooses on the new `f8962.income_100` (line 5 at least 100): true takes it, false takes `f8962.estimate_exception`, a choice on `f8962.aptc` that reads `f8962.estimate_100` only when advance payments were made. `f8962.alien_branch` chooses on `f8962.any`, then `f8962.alien_from_income`, which reads `f8962.alien_below` only when `f8962.income_100` is false (`f8962.alien_branch` now tests the same line 5 helper, so "below 100" is its negation; the separate `lt` comparison and its mutants are gone). `f8962.b_zero` chooses on `f8962.show_applicable` and reads the twelve month tests, unchanged and moved to `f8962.b_zero_month`, only for an applicable taxpayer. The four helper lines are at the end of the document's lines, each with the citation of the line it serves. The three BUG-0487 holds are removed from `walked_unused`: the baseline holds nothing.
- **Fix lines:** `f8962.applicable`, `f8962.alien_branch`, `f8962.b_zero`
- **Siblings checked:** `f8962.filing`, `f8962.show_applicable`, `f8962.line24`, `f8962.show_annual_calc`, `f8962.show_jan_calc`, `f8962.show_feb_calc`, `f8962.show_mar_calc`, `f8962.show_apr_calc`, `f8962.show_may_calc`, `f8962.show_jun_calc`, `f8962.show_jul_calc`, `f8962.show_aug_calc`, `f8962.show_sep_calc`, `f8962.show_oct_calc`, `f8962.show_nov_calc`, `f8962.show_dec_calc` (the readers of `f8962.applicable`; its value on every complete return is unchanged, no change; `f8962.show_applicable` and `f8962.filing` are conjunctions on `f8962.any` and computed lines only and read no question out of turn), `f8962.line25` (with `f8962.line24` the reader of the gate `f8962.alien_branch`; no change), `f8962.two_counted` (the reader of `f8962.b_zero`; no change)
- **Regression predictions:** no complete return's value or refusal changes. On incomplete states a value the three-valued `all` or `any` decided from a later operand is unknown until the earlier operand is known (the trade-off the owner accepted in BUG-0471): on the evaluator's own truth tables over true, false, unknown, gate-pending and refused operands, the old and new line agree wherever every operand is known, and every difference has an unknown operand before the deciding one and is unknown afterwards. No asserted fixture holds such a state.
- **Validation:** Each family alone and the four of this round together (BUG-0603, BUG-0604): every federal and New York fixture passes with no expected value, refusal or completion changed (the class M cases of dependent and f8962 were regenerated by this round's class M reviews); status and every target value are identical to main on 3,000 generated returns (712 complete; 1,500 for each family alone) and on every fixture's inputs. Evaluator truth tables as stated under Regression predictions. Sweep of 2,000 generated returns (40 seeds of 50; 449 complete), return by return against main: status differs on none and no order error; `f8962.applicable` and `f8962.alien_branch` alone save 103 questions on 51 complete returns and `f8962.b_zero` alone 98 on 5, none longer; every template BUG-0487 and BUG-0601 name is gone. The three hand-built returns of BUG-0601 are walked in 99, 97 and 97 questions where main asks 112, 121 and 115, none unread. `interview-rules` reports only the three stale holds before they are removed and 0 problems after; on the interview-length set one complete return is shorter (generated.4, 261 to 258) and none longer. Mutation: no survivor unexplained. Six pinned arguments whose premises changed were re-read against the new expressions and hold as written (`f8962.filing` reading `f8962.show_applicable`; the false alternatives of `dependent.qr_dependent`, `dependent.qr_kidnapped` and `dependent.eic_ssn_child`; the married gate of `dependent.qualifying_relative`; `dependent.dc_line2c`), and five new survivors on the new lines have pinned arguments (the false alternatives of `dependent.qualifying_relative`, `dependent.odc_person`, `dependent.odc_from_tin`, `f8962.alien_branch` and `f8962.estimate_exception`); each of the eleven was also compared with the unmutated data on 3,000 generated returns with answers withheld at six rates, every line but the mutated one, with no difference beyond the one the argument on the married gate already names. Reviews (claude-fable-5-2; cost stated in BUG-0603): transcription and render (line-scoped) and class M of f8962. Render: one mismatch on line 24, the married-filing-separately reading ruled scope before (s3.mfs refuses the return). Class M: 181 lines agree, one model error on line 4 of one case (the poverty line for a family of 1 entered for a family of 2), dropped from the fixture. Transcription: 89 lines disagree, all ruled, none a finding; no value differs on a completed return, and every difference there is a line the project hides or an answer the interview does not ask. Made due and not run, as a sampled review: the question `f8962.alien_below` (next full pass).
- **Tags:** interview; leak; conjunction; order-dependence; fixed

## BUG-0605 — Two fixture cases carry line-level refusals only because a test-data default is not a truthful answer for them

(Replaces the draft `/tmp/qfix/t269/bug_defaults_body.md`: its third case, `ss.hoh`, is dealt with under T-277 and is no longer part of this entry; see the note at the end.)

- **Date:** 2026-11-11
- **Caught by:** the T-269 audit of `fixtures/2025/defaults.json`; re-run under T-277 (each case evaluated with the answer withheld and with it answered yes, every line compared).
- **Source:** `fixtures/2025/defaults.json` answers `dependent.edu_tin_issued` no for every student that does not state it. For a lifetime learning credit student that answer fires the refusal `dependent.edu_llc_tin_refused` (i8863 p. 3, Who cannot claim a credit, item 5). Both students also take `dependent.tin` yes by default, so the no says "an ITIN or ATIN was only applied for", which neither case's scenario is about.
- **Symptom:** (1) `stage19.mut.claimed_filer_llc` (the filer is claimed as a dependent; lines 10 and 11 are $0): `dependent[daughter].edu_line31`, `f8863.llc_dep` and `f8863.llc_sum` are refused at `dependent[daughter].edu_llc_tin_refused`. (2) `stage19.mut.classm_f5329_3_dependent_no_ein` (the institution's EIN is missing): the same on `dependent[dep_a].edu_line31` and Form 8863 lines 10, 11, 12, `llc_dep` and `llc_sum`, and 12 further lines (Form 1040 line 20, Form 8863 lines 18 and 19 and credit limit worksheet lines 1, 3 and 7, Schedule 3 lines 3 and 8, two Form 5695 worksheet lines, a Form 8880 and a Schedule 8812 worksheet line) name `dependent[dep_a].edu_llc_tin_refused` as their refusal where `sa.excluded_income` is named otherwise. No asserted value, return state, return target or interview status depends on the answer in either case.
- **Where:** `fixtures/2025/f8863.json` (`stage19.mut.claimed_filer_llc`), `fixtures/2025/dependent.json` (`stage19.mut.classm_f5329_3_dependent_no_ein`).
- **Severity:** low (no asserted value is wrong; the cases' unasserted lines show a refusal their scenarios do not mean, and a review that reads the answer differs from the project there).
- **Status:** open. The withholding condition on `dependent.edu_tin_issued` (T-277) covers only a student whose answers allow the American opportunity credit, so these two keep the default. The fix is to state `edu_tin_issued: true` in both cases; it changes the lines above from refused to $0 (first case) or to the `sa.excluded_income` refusal (second case), which is a change of a refusal and so is left for a decision.
- **Tags:** fixtures; defaults; test-data; refusal; open

Note on `ss.hoh` (`fixtures/2025/s3.json`): the T-269 draft said a truthful `household.unmarried` would change that return's refusal. Run under T-277: stating `household.unmarried: true` changes no line, return state, return target or interview status of the case (the return is refused at `household.hoh_fails` either way). The case now states it. What remains true of the case is that it asserts Schedule 3 lines of a head of household whose return is refused at the head-of-household tests; whether to give it a qualifying person and the cost of the home is a separate, smaller question and is not drafted as a bug here.

## BUG-0606 — The test-data defaults give contradictory birth-date answers, and six education credit cases rest on them

- **Date:** 2026-11-11
- **Caught by:** the T-269 audit; made mechanical by the consistency rules of T-277 (`fixtures/2025/defaults.json`, `consistency`, rules 3 and 4), which the build reads on every case.
- **Source:** the defaults answer `person.born_before_2001` yes (the filer of the defaults is 25 or older, the earned income credit's minimum age) and `person.edu_born_2002` and `person.edu_born_2007` no (Form 8863 line 7's age tests). A person born before January 2, 2001 was born before January 2, 2002 and before January 2, 2007.
- **Symptom:** every person entry that takes the three defaults is at once 25 or older and under 18. Four completed returns read the no answers as facts of their scenario without stating them (`stage19.blind.e6`, `stage19.blind.e7`, `stage19.blind.e8`, `stage19.mut.aoc_student_18_half_support`: withholding the two defaults for a person born before January 2, 2001 makes each incomplete, with Form 8863 lines 8 and 9 and about 50 lines after them unknown). Two cases state `edu_born_2002: false` and take `born_before_2001: true` (`stage19.mut.aoc_student_20_not_fulltime`, `stage19.mut.aoc_joint_line7_unasked`). No ruled reviewer value difference has been traced to these answers.
- **Where:** `fixtures/2025/defaults.json` (the three defaults), `fixtures/2025/f8863.json` (the six cases).
- **Severity:** low (no asserted value is wrong).
- **Status:** open; the rules list the defaults themselves (rules 3 and 4) and the two stating cases (rule 3) as `open`, so the build is green and any new case that states one of the answers against a default is refused. Tried under T-277 and not kept: (a) withholding `edu_born_2002` and `edu_born_2007` in the defaults for a person born before January 2, 2001 changes four returns from completed to incomplete; (b) stating the truthful `born_before_2001: false` in the two stating cases changes the values of their earned income credit lines (`eic.age_range_count`, and in one case `eic.age_range`, `eic.step4_age`, `eic.step4`, `eic.step34` from yes to no), with no return state, return target or interview status change; withholding it instead makes the same lines unknown. A fix that keeps every asserted value: state `edu_born_2002` and `edu_born_2007` in the four reading cases as their scenarios mean, state `born_before_2001: false` in all six, accept the earned income credit line changes, then make the two education defaults yes (or withhold them for a person born before January 2, 2001) and drop the `open` entries.
- **Tags:** fixtures; defaults; test-data; consistency; open

## BUG-0607 — The interview's opening asked one fact three or four times and showed the filing status as codes

- **Date:** 2026-11-11
- **Caught by:** the owner, walking his own return in the web UI (docs/2026-11-11_owner_walkthrough_notes.md, note 1): "isn't question 3 answerable from both previous question's answers?"
- **Symptom:** the first three questions of the whole return asked one fact three or four times. `$person` ("Who is on this return: just you, or you and your spouse on a joint return?") created the entries and labelled them; `f1040.status` was shown as the bare label "Form 1040, Filing Status checkboxes" with no help and the model's codes (`single`, `mfj`, `mfs`, `hoh`, `qss`) as its options, although "Me and my spouse (joint return)" had already said married filing jointly; and `person.role` then asked of each entry "Whose entry is this, yours (the taxpayer) or your spouse's?", twice on a joint return. Each could be answered against the first, and the tool then reported a conflict (`household.roster_bad`). Every per-person question began "For this person (you, or your spouse on a joint return) — ", on a one-person return too.
- **Source:** Form 1040 (2025), page 1, Filing Status, "Married filing jointly (even if only one had income)"; i1040gi pp. 13 to 15, Filing Status (the tests of each status, "More than one filing status can apply to you", Married persons who live apart).
- **Where:** `interview/2025/questions.yaml` (`$person`, `f1040.status`, `person.role`), `engine/src/interview.ts`, `engine/src/spouse-wording.ts`, `engine/src/serve.ts`, `ui/app.ts`; the rule "the interview sets no input" in `engine/src/interview-rules.ts`.
- **Severity:** medium (no value was wrong; every filer read 58 to 82 words to say who is on the return, a couple could contradict the first answer twice, and the filing status could not be chosen without knowing the codes).
- **Disposition:** fixed (T-282, the opening of the interview redesign's first slice; owner decisions 1, 2 and 7 of docs/2026-11-11_interview_redesign_slice_design.md, section H). (1) `$person` asks "Who is this tax return for?" with "Just me" or "Me and my husband or wife, together on one return". (2) A roster choice may record answers its label states, declared beside the choice in the bank (`records`): each entry's `person.role`, and, for the couple, `f1040.status` = `mfj`. The rule is restated, not removed: a choice records only inputs of the entries it creates or the one input on the allow-list `RECORD_ALLOWED` (`f1040.status` as `mfj`, by the couple's choice), at a value the input can take; the build and `interview-rules` enforce it, and its self-test flags a violation of each limit (14). One function, `answerEvent`, attaches the records, and the CLI, the server and every walk (fixtures, generated returns, tests) answer through it; the records are saved on the answer's event and replay applies them from the event. A recorded answer cannot be answered directly; changing the choice withdraws what the old choice recorded (interview/README.md, "Answers a choice records"). `person.role` stays an input of the model, read by 33 lines, and has no question. (3) `f1040.status` is asked only of one person, as "Which of these fits you on December 31, 2025?", with four situations each followed by the official name, in the bank's order; married filing jointly, which only the couple's choice records, is not offered. (4) Married filing separately is still refused at once (`s3.mfs`), now with a note in plain words (`interview/2025/refusal_notes.yaml`); a failed head of household or qualifying surviving spouse choice has one too. The form data's refusal text is unchanged. (5) The per-person frame is shown as "About you" or "About your spouse" on a return with two people and not at all on a return with one; the stored text is unchanged.
- **Regression predictions:** no form line, fixture, default or expected value changes. A log answered under the earlier questions replays to the same state. The interview asks one question fewer of one person and three fewer of a couple.
- **Validation:** `interview-rules` reports 0 problems (177 walks) before and after; with `INTERVIEW_RULES_RUNS=200` it reports 12 before and 12 after, the same two asked-and-unread templates and ten templates reached only out of bank order, nine of them the same: `person.died_before_65` is no longer reported and `f8889.last_month` is. Neither difference is a new leak: on the unchanged tree a random answering order reaches `f8889.last_month` on generated return 77 in 1 of 60 seeded orders (2 of 60 after), so the five orders of a run seldom show it; and `person.died_before_65` was reached on generated return 198 only while a role was unanswered (11 of 60 orders before, none of 60 after), a state the interview no longer has. `test-integration` walks the opening at the command line (the couple, a changed choice both ways, a help request, refused direct answers, and logs of the earlier questions giving the same state); `test-serve` does the same through the server and compares it with the command line; `ui/test_browser.mjs` passes; screenshots of the first screen, the status screen and a per-person question on each kind of return were read. The question review of `f1040.status` and `person.role` was run on the new wording: its first round found two real defects of the draft wording, fixed before the second (the head of household line stood above the qualifying surviving spouse line, so a filer meeting both took the first; the first question's help could be read as needing both spouses to have income); the second round found `person.role` MATCH and one case for `f1040.status` that the return refuses (a nonresident alien spouse, `scope.other_income`).
- **Tags:** interview; redesign; opening; no-input-set; tool change; fixed

## BUG-0608 — The question review judged a labelled enum question by its value codes, not the lines the filer chooses among

- **Date:** 2026-11-11
- **Caught by:** the opening lane of T-282, preparing the question review of `f1040.status` after its options were given labels.
- **Symptom:** the question review (`tools/transcription/question_review.py`) gave its reviewer "the question as the filer reads it", but for an enum question it listed the model's value codes ("Enum filing_status: one of single, mfj, mfs, hoh, qss") and not the labels the filer chooses among (`value_labels`), and it knew nothing of an answer that is recorded by a roster choice and not asked. A review of a labelled enum therefore never judged the words a filer reads, and its subject did not change when a label did. Four built questions have labels: `f1040.status`, `f8889.coverage_year`, `f8889.dec_coverage`, `f8962.fpl_table`.
- **Where:** `tools/transcription/question_review.py` (`questions_of`, `build_prompt`).
- **Severity:** low (a review that could not see part of its subject; no finding was wrong).
- **Disposition:** fixed. The question as the reviewer reads it now lists a labelled enum's options in the order shown, each with its value, and, for an input a roster choice records, the other question, its help, and each choice's label with the value it records; an input that is recorded and never asked (`person.role`) is reviewed through those choices. Both are part of the question's subject, so a changed label or record makes the question due.
- **Regression predictions:** the subjects of the labelled questions change. `f1040.status` and `person.role` are reviewed in this change. `f8962.fpl_table` and `f8889.dec_coverage` become due at the next full pass without any change of their own (`f8889.coverage_year` was already due, never reviewed); under the owner's rule that a tool change applies prospectively they are not rerun here.
- **Validation:** `question_review.py --self-test`; the prompts written for `f1040.status` and `person.role` (`--measure --write-prompts`) were read; `check_questions.py` lists 159 questions due (157 before: the two above added; `f1040.status` and `person.role` reviewed and current).
- **Tags:** tool change; review process; question review; fixed

## BUG-0609 — A question shown About your spouse said you of the spouse, and this person had no referent where the frame is dropped

- **Date:** 2026-11-11
- **Caught by:** the opening lane of T-282, reading screenshots of per-person questions on a couple's return and on one person's; fixed on the owner's decision of 2026-11-12 (before landing, at display time, checked by the build).
- **Symptom:** the per-person frame was shown as "About you" or "About your spouse" (and not at all on a return with one person), but the questions beneath it kept the wording written for the old frame. (1) On a couple's return a question about the spouse still said "you": "About your spouse — Were you under age 16 at the end of 2025?". The old frame, "For this person (you, or your spouse on a joint return) — Were you ...", had the same fault. 74 of the 84 framed questions say "you", "your", "yours" or "yourself" in their prompt or help. (2) On a return with one person, where the frame is dropped, "this person" had nothing left to refer to; 11 texts of 11 framed questions say it (prompts: `$retirement`, `person.edu`, `person.se_screen`, `person.plan`, `f8889.allocated`, `f8889.unsupported`; helps: `person.rrta`, `person.age65`, `person.blind`, `person.itin_applied`, `person.sav_claimed`).
- **Where:** `engine/src/spouse-wording.ts` (`personWording`, `shownFor`), `engine/src/build.ts`; `interview/2025/questions.yaml` (the help of `person.rrta`); new `reports/2025/person_wording.md`.
- **Severity:** low (no answer changed; a hurried reader of "About your spouse — Were you ..." could answer for themselves).
- **Disposition:** fixed, by a display-time rule beside the frame's (interview/README.md, "The person a question is about, as shown"). A framed question is stored in the second person and shown for the entry it is asked of. For the spouse's entry: "you" as a subject becomes "your spouse" with the verb after it agreeing ("you have" to "your spouse has", "Were you" to "Was your spouse", a second verb after "or"/"and" and a verb after an apposition too); "you" as an object becomes "your spouse"; "your" and "yours" become "your spouse's"; "yourself" becomes "himself or herself"; "this person" becomes "your spouse"; and "your spouse", the husband or wife of the person asked about, becomes "you" ("a joint return with your spouse" to "a joint return with you"). For the taxpayer's entry only "this person" changes, to "you". A phrase that means both people ("you and your spouse", "you or your spouse", "you both", "either of you", "both of you") is shown as stored. The rule works from closed lists; the build fails, naming the question and the words, on a framed prompt or help it does not cover: a subject before a word in neither list, a contraction, or a changing verb after a preposition's object. One stored text was reworded because the rule could not cover it: the help of `person.rrta`, "any Form W-2 of this person reports" to "any of this person's Forms W-2 reports". Since the reviews read the stored text, the shown text has its own record: `reports/2025/person_wording.md` lists every framed question as stored and in each shown form, and check-all fails when it is not current.
- **Regression predictions:** no form line, expression, refusal text, fixture or default changes. The stored text of one help changes (`person.rrta`).
- **Validation:** `spouse-wording --self-test` (14 constructed texts, one for each row of the rule, in both forms; 6 uncovered wordings each refused; all 84 built framed questions covered, and well-formed in each shown form with no "this person" left); the build check found the one uncovered built text before it was reworded; every shown form of the 84 questions was read in the report. Read and judged awkward but acceptable: `person.plan_screen` ("contributions for himself or herself to more than one plan", with only the frame as antecedent); `person.sav_prior_other` (its parenthesis about a return that is not joint, which a spouse's entry never is); the education questions that say "the student" and `person.died_before_65` ("a person born between ..."), which are stored in the third person and unchanged. Two Form 8889 questions use "you" for the couple and so read wrongly for the spouse's entry until they are rewritten in the same slice: `f8889.allocation` ("Does your spouse divide the family contribution limit ...") and `f8889.allocated` ("the allocation your spouse agreed on").
- **Tags:** interview; wording; per-person frame; display rule; fixed

## BUG-0611 — Money paid out of, or rolled over from, an Archer MSA was caught by no question

- **Date:** 2026-11-12
- **Caught by:** the redesign's design (docs/2026-11-11_interview_redesign_slice_design.md, A.3 finding 5), reading i8889 and i8853 against `f8889.unsupported`.
- **Source:** i8853 p. 1, Who Must File, "You (or your spouse, if filing jointly) received Archer MSA or Medicare Advantage MSA distributions in 2025"; i8889 p. 3, Rollovers, "from one HSA or Archer MSA".
- **Symptom:** the catch-all named only contributions to an Archer MSA, so a person with a health savings account who was paid from an Archer MSA, or rolled one into the HSA, answered No and the return was completed without Form 8853.
- **Where:** `forms/2025/f8889.yaml`.
- **Fix:** `f8889.archer` asks whether the person or the spouse had an Archer MSA in 2025 and refuses line 13 on Yes. Wider than before: the spouse's Archer MSA refuses whatever the coverage, and so does an Archer MSA nothing went into or came out of (open entry below).
- **Fix lines:** `f8889.line13`
- **Siblings checked:** `f8889.archer`, `f8889.inherited`, `f8889.line16`, `f8889.no_last_month`, `f8889.owner_died`, `f8889.use_last_month` (line 16 does not read the Archer MSA question and is not refused by it; the others cite the same passage and are unchanged)
- **Validation:** fixture `redesign.hsa.refuse.archer`; coverage rows `hsa.archer_msa` and `hsa.archer_msa_payout`.
- **Tags:** interview; Form 8889; Archer MSA; refusal; fixed
