## BUG-0640 — scope.recovery leaves out recoveries of an amount taken as a credit, and refuses a local income tax refund that the refund form prepares

- **Caught by:** landing adjudication lane land3-adj10 (Claude render log of scope, line recovery, pass 1b4bf43be4e1, UNCLEAR), 2026-11-14.
- **Source:** p525 p. 24, Recoveries, "A recovery is a return of an amount you deducted or took a credit for in an earlier year" and Tax benefit rule, "up to the amount by which the deduction or credit you took for the recovered amount reduced your tax in the earlier year"; f1040s1 line 1, "Taxable refunds, credits, or offsets of state and local income taxes".
- **Symptom:** The question (label and input source) asks only about an amount "whose deduction on an earlier year's return lowered your tax, other than a state income tax refund" (tick: "Paid back a deduction that lowered your tax (not a state refund)"). (1) A filer who got back an amount for which an earlier credit lowered the tax reads the question literally and answers No; the recovery is then left out of Schedule 1 line 8z with no refusal: a wrong completed return (rare). (2) A filer whose only recovery is a local (city or county) income tax refund is told the exception covers only a state refund, answers Yes and is refused, although the refund form (refund.any: "state or local income tax") prepares it: an unneeded refusal.
- **Where:** forms/2025/scope.yaml: scope.recovery (label and expr.source); interview/2025/questions.yaml: scope.recovery tick (order 161, seq 6, group money_b).
- **Fix:** (landing round, before re-review) the question, label and source of `scope.recovery` now ask about an amount whose deduction or credit lowered an earlier year's tax, other than a state or local income tax refund; the citation moves from a generic Form 1040 locator to p525 p. 24, Recoveries ("A recovery is a return of an amount you deducted or took a credit for in an earlier year"); the bank tick reads "Paid back a deduction or credit that lowered tax (not state/local refund)" (12 words) and the help says a state or local income tax refund is asked about separately. No expression changed.
- **Fix lines:** `scope.recovery`
- **Siblings checked:** `scope.schedule1` (the only reader; it reads the answer unchanged, so a Yes still refuses there and a local income tax refund now answers No and reaches `refund.any`, which prepares it)
- **Regression predictions:** no fixture value changes (text only); the line-scoped transcription and render reviews of `scope.recovery` rerun in this round; the question and screen reviews of the changed text are due at the next sample.
- **Proposed fix (as drafted by the adjudicator):** scope.recovery label and source: "In 2025, were you (or, on a joint return, your spouse) paid back an amount whose deduction or credit on an earlier year's return lowered your tax, other than a state or local income tax refund?"; tick: "Paid back a deduction or credit that lowered your tax (not a state or local income tax refund)"; cite p525 p. 24, Recoveries and Tax benefit rule, in place of the generic Form 1040 locator. Help unchanged. No expression change; rerun the scope render review at the form's next change.
- **Tags:** interview wording; scope screen; medium

## BUG-0641 — Class M jobs for a New York form give the rate-schedule results as unnamed line (39)/(47a) amounts and leave the Tax Table lookup unworkable

- **Caught by:** landing adjudication lane land3-adj11 (Claude class M log of ny_it201, cases 1, 2, 3, 4 and 6, 75 of 97 disagreements), 2026-11-14.
- **Source:** sources/ny/2025/ny_it201_tax_tables.txt (the 2025 New York State and City Tax Tables), e.g. row 32,000 to 32,050: State 1,597 (single and MFS), City 1,126; IT-201-I p. 12, Line 39, "find your New York State tax using the 2025 New York State Tax Table"; tools/transcription/README.md, class M: "Results of the shared tax computation (Tax Table or Tax Computation Worksheet) are given, not worked".
- **Symptom:** Each ny_it201 class M prompt gives fourteen amounts all named "this document, line (39)" and one "this document, line (47a)", noted "result of the shared tax computation (Tax Table or Tax Computation Worksheet)". They are the results of the form's own definition instances (ny_rs, ny_tcw, ny_city_rs), i.e. the rate schedule applied to the exact amount ($1,596 State and $1,125 City at $32,000), not the Tax Table, whose rows are taxed at their midpoint ($1,597 and $1,126). The Tax Table lines ny_it201.tax_table and ny_it201.city_tax_table (op table_lookup) are not given and are left to the model, but the tables are not among the source pages, so the model copies a given (39)/(47a) amount and is $1 off on line 39 or 47a and on every line below them (44, 46, 47a, 49, 52, 54, 58, 61, 62, 80). No return is affected (the engine matches the published table on all five cases); the cost is false disagreements in every New York class M run of ny_it201, and a fixture that would assert the wrong values unless each is dropped.
- **Where:** engine/src/classm.ts buildJob: the given "shared tax computation" results are the document's definition lines only (defLines from walk), not its table_lookup lines over the tax tables; tools/transcription/classm.py given_name: a line of this document is named by its printed number alone, so several helpers printed (39) are indistinguishable.
- **Proposed fix:** (1) In buildJob, give a table_lookup line over a tax table (ny_tax_table, ny_city_tax_table, and any table the README counts as the shared tax computation) as a shared-computation result, like a definition line, and drop it from the lines to fill; (2) in given_name, name a line of this document by its handle (printed and id where the printed number is shared, as classm.handle does) and its label. Then rerun ny_it201 class M at its next real change; the 75 lines of this round were dropped.
- **Tags:** tool change; class M; New York; low

## BUG-0642 — Net operating loss from a personal casualty is gated behind a business question

- **Date:** 2026-11-14.
- **Caught by:** the consumers check on the landing branch (tools/check_consumers.py): the pair was drafted as "differs" by an Opus reading agent of the landing lane (claude-opus-5-5, judgment), 2026-11-14, and left unruled; not yet checked by a second reader.
- **Source:** i1040gi p. 91, Line 8a.
- **Symptom:** scope.nol is asked only after scope.business_before; a filer whose carried loss came from a personal casualty or theft and who never had a business answers No and never reaches scope.nol, whose own help says such a loss counts. Pair consumer:scope.business_before@i1040gi:p91.
- **Tags:** interview wording, scope, consumers
- **Fix:** The source was checked: i1040gi p. 91, Line 8a, "Enter any deduction for an NOL from an earlier year", states no business condition and sends the reader to the Instructions for Form 172. That an individual's NOL can come from a personal casualty or theft loss is NOL law (section 172(d)(4)(C)); no source in `sources/2025` states it, so that part rests on the reading agent's and this lane's knowledge, not a quoted page. `scope.nol` is no longer gated: the gate line `scope.nol_if_business_before` is removed, and `scope.schedule1` reads `scope.nol` directly (same place in its `any`), so every filer is asked it and a Yes refuses Schedule 1 as before. Its question gains the spouse phrase ("Are you (or, on a joint return, your spouse) carrying a loss from an earlier year into 2025 as a 'net operating loss' deduction?"), since a spouse's carryover goes on a joint return, and it now cites i1040gi p. 91, Line 8a, in place of the generic Form 1040 locator. The parent was not widened (N2: a parent that could be answered No wrongly is remedied by a separate question, never a longer parent). So that the typical filer takes no extra step, `scope.business_before` and `scope.nol` are one tick-box screen, `before_2025` ("Before 2025, did you (or, on a joint return, your spouse) have either of these?"), boxes "A business, farm, rental, or share in a partnership or S corporation" (seq 1) and "A loss still being carried into 2025 (a 'net operating loss')" (seq 2). The help of `scope.nol` now says what the loss is and that it can come from a disaster or theft with no business.
- **Fix lines:** `scope.nol`, `scope.schedule1`
- **Siblings checked:** `scope.schedule1` (now reads scope.nol directly; true for the casualty-NOL filer, who was wrongly computed before), `eic.clergy`, `eic.step2_other` (test scope.schedule1; a filer refused at Schedule 1 is refused there in any case, unchanged), `oi8z.additional_tax`, `oi8z.amount`, `oi8z.figured`, `oi8z.kind`, `oi8z.recovery`, `oi8z.taxable`, `s1.line8z` (share the i1040gi p. 91 and 92 anchors for other income items; do not read scope.nol; unchanged), `person.se_screen` (shares the i1040sse anchor; unchanged), `scope.artist_official_if_w2`, `scope.church_exempt_wages_if_religious_work`, `scope.clergy_if_religious_work`, `scope.military_move_if_armed_forces`, `scope.performer_expenses_if_artist_official`, `scope.reservist_expenses_if_armed_forces`, `scope.se_plan_other_if_business`, `scope.w2_marks_if_w2` (the other gated screening items of scope.schedule1; each parent names its own item's population, no one of them asked about a loss carried in; unchanged), `scope.nol` (the fix's own line). Also read: `scope.passive_if_business_before`, `scope.f8978_if_business_before`, `s179.prior_form_if_before` (the other children of scope.business_before; a passive loss carried over, a Form 8986 and a section 179 carryover all need a holding before 2025, so they stay beneath it).
- **Regression predictions:** no expected value changes. Every filer now answers `scope.nol`; on the page it shares one screen with `scope.business_before`, so the step count is unchanged for the filer with no business and one fewer for a filer with one. The class M files take no defaults: 11 cases (`classm.eic.1` to `classm.eic.11`) that answered `scope.business_before` No and never stated `scope.nol` now state it false; no scenario has a carried loss. New case `scope.reg.nol_casualty_no_business` (fixtures/2025/scope.json), predicted before running: the inputs of `stage4.refuse.scope.schedule1` with no rental, no business before 2025 and `scope.nol` Yes; predicted `scope.ready` refused on `scope.schedule1` with the Schedule 1 remedy; result matched. Before the fix the same answers gave `scope.nol_if_business_before` false and no Schedule 1 refusal (inferred from the removed gate's definition; not run on the old tree). Coverage row `scope.nol_casualty_no_business` (interview/2025/coverage/scope.yaml) walks the same case.

## BUG-0643 — ISO stock that vests in 2025 after an earlier exercise is not caught

- **Date:** 2026-11-14.
- **Caught by:** the consumers check on the landing branch (tools/check_consumers.py): the pair was drafted as "differs" by an Opus reading agent of the landing lane (claude-opus-5-5, judgment), 2026-11-14, and left unruled; not yet checked by a second reader.
- **Source:** i6251 p. 4, Line 2i; i6251 p. 1, Who Must File.
- **Symptom:** s2.options_any and s2.iso ask about options exercised in 2025; the AMT adjustment arises in the year the stock becomes transferable or vested, so an earlier exercise with 2025 vesting answers No to both. Pairs consumer:s2.iso@i6251:p1/p4 and consumer:s2.options_any@i6251:p1/p4.
- **Tags:** interview wording, scope, consumers
- **Fix:** The source was checked: i6251 p. 4, Line 2i, measures the adjustment at the stock's value "when your rights in the acquired stock first become transferable or when these rights are no longer subject to a substantial risk of forfeiture", unless the filer elected to include it "upon the transfer to you" (within 30 days). Stock bought before 2025 that vests in 2025 therefore gives a 2025 adjustment, and `s2.options_any` and `s2.iso` (both about 2025 exercises) miss it. A new input `s2.iso_vested` ("Did shares that you (or, on a joint return, your spouse) bought before 2025 with incentive stock options vest in 2025, that is, first become yours to sell or no longer able to be forfeited?"), cited to i6251 p. 4, Line 2i, and p. 1, Who Must File, is asked of every filer, and `s2.amt` reads it beside `s2.iso_if_options` and `s2.amt_owed`, so a Yes reaches the same Form 6251 refusal as a 2025 exercise. The parent `s2.options_any` was not widened (N2): the case is a sixth box of the existing screen `other_pay` (order 146, seq 6), "Shares bought before 2025 with incentive stock options that vested in 2025", prompt "Did shares you (or, on a joint return, your spouse) bought before 2025 with incentive stock options (ISOs) vest in 2025?", help naming the early exercise and telling a filer who made the 30-day election to answer No. `s2.iso` is unchanged: it catches the 2025 exercise; its Yes for stock still unvested at the end of 2025 only refuses.
- **Fix lines:** `s2.iso_vested`, `s2.amt`
- **Siblings checked:** `s2.amt` (reads the new input; one more Yes refuses), `s2.iso_if_options` (anchored on i6251 p. 1 and p. 4; reads s2.options_any and s2.iso; unchanged, the 2025 exercise), `s2.iso_vested` (the fix's own line). Also read: `s2.iso`, `s2.options_any` (unchanged; their consumer pairs at i6251 p. 1 and p. 4 re-ruled same, naming the new sibling), `s1.stock_options_if_options` (reads s2.options_any for line 8k; unaffected), `s2.amt_owed` (unchanged; its question still says "other than from incentive stock options exercised in 2025", which leaves a vesting filer who reads it free to say Yes as well; left as a residual wording point), the refusals on `s2.line2`, `s2.line3`, `s2.line21` (gate s2.amt; unchanged).
- **Regression predictions:** no expected value changes. Every filer who reaches the `other_pay` screen sees one more box (12 words); no step is added. The class M and mutation files take no defaults: 92 cases (44 in classm.json, 40 in classm.deepseek.json, 8 in mutation.json) now state `s2.iso_vested` false; no scenario has ISO stock vesting in 2025. New case `s2.reg.iso_vested_2025` (fixtures/2025/s2.json), predicted before running: the inputs of `stage4.refuse.s2.amt` with `s2.amt_owed` No, `s2.options_any` No and `s2.iso_vested` Yes; predicted `s2.line2`, `s2.line3` and `s2.line21` refused on `s2.amt` (Form 6251); result matched (3 values). Before the fix no question asked this, and the same filer was computed without Form 6251. Coverage row `other.iso_vested_2025` (interview/2025/coverage/other.yaml).

## BUG-0644 — Year operations that remove a refusal gate or an input are not checked against the year-shared files that name it

- **Date:** 2026-11-14.
- **Caught by:** lane O5 of the TY2026 preparation (claude-opus-5-5, judgment), writing changes/2026/person.edu.yaml and dependent.edu.yaml.
- **Symptom:** The 2026 operations remove the refusal gates person.edu_llc_tin_refused and dependent.edu_llc_tin_refused and the input dependent.edu_tin_issued (C-CRED-18, C-PEOP-16), and year_changes.py --check passes. But tools/coverage/tree.json, which is not kept per year, still places both gates (lines 265-266), so tools/coverage/tree.py --check on the adopted 2026 build would fail with 'placed in tree.json but no refusal in the forms uses it'; and tools/engines/generate_cases.py (line 856) still sets dependent[k].edu_tin_issued for every generated dependent, an input 2026 no longer has (its effect on a 2026 run not tried). The check's dangling rule covers lines, questions, profiles and the files under interview/<year>/, not these year-shared files. Other lanes' removals (Form 5695 Part I and II, C-CRED-02 to -08) meet the same.
- **Tags:** tool change, year changes, adoption
- **Fix (proposed):** Either key tree.json's gate placements by year (or let a placement name the years it holds for), and make generate_cases.py set only inputs the year's build defines; or extend year_changes.py's dangling rule to report every removed id still named in tools/coverage/tree.json and tools/engines/generate_cases.py, so the operation lane sees it before adoption.
- **Tool change:** Fixed in the adoption tooling by lane R6 (claude-opus-5-5, judgment), 2026-11-14, by listing, the third design of the three weighed. New `tools/year_shared_refs.py` applies the year's operations (through `year_changes.check`) and lists every reference, in code and tool data kept for every year (Python, TypeScript, JavaScript, JSON and shell under `tools/` and `engine/src/`, not under a year directory), to a line the operations remove or to a refusal gate that no refusal uses after them. A reference is the id itself (also inside a key, such as a mutation pin `operand.f5695.f5695.part1_any.no.then1`, but not run into a longer id), an instance id (`dependent[{k}].edu_tin_issued`), the local name as a quoted string in a file that builds the form's ids from names (`f"f5695.{k}"`, a weaker match), or a coverage-tree `"gate"` placement of a retired gate. `year_changes.py --check` notes the count, so an operation lane sees it before adoption; `year_diff.py --adopt` writes `reports/<to>/shared_refs_from_<from>.{json,md}`. Measured with this tree's changes/2026 plus O5's five files, O3a's f5695.yaml and R3's staged person.ambiguity.yaml (copied in for the run and removed): 412 references in 8 files: tools/coverage/tree.json 16 (both edu gates at lines 265 and 266, and the 14 f5695 gates of lines 269 to 282), tools/engines/generate_cases.py 143 (the `dependent[k].edu_tin_issued` instance at line 856 among them; 82 weak), engine/src/generate.ts 138 (100 weak), engine/src/mutate.ts 88, run_engines.py 11, compare.py 8, ots_adapter.py 5, ustaxes_adapter.py 3. That covers every file and line range of lane O3a's list. With this tree's own changes/2026 (which removes f1040.line28_box and scveh.rate) the list is empty.
  Why listing: a per-year copy of tree.json would fit the coverage tree, but the generators, mutation pins and adapters are code, and a per-year copy of code is not maintainable. Reading ids from the year's build with a silent skip would hide drift: a renamed id would simply stop being generated, and coverage would fall without a failure. A shared file serves both years at once (2025 still needs Part II of Form 5695), so what each file does for the new year (a year branch, a skip of ids the year lacks, a removal when the old year retires) is a judgment per file that only the adoption lane can make; the list gives it every place to decide, at the cost of a two-second scan. The list does not refuse adoption; the coordinator may make a non-empty list a failure of the adoption lane's check-all if that is wanted.
- **Tool files:** tools/year_shared_refs.py (new: `shared_files`, `gates_of`, `lost_ids`, `scan`, `references`, `write_report`, `self_test`, `main`); tools/year_changes.py `check` (one note block after the evidence check); tools/year_diff.py `adopt` (one block after the operations are applied); tools/self_tests.py (the self-test registered); tools/tier_paths.py (WALKERS entry for its `.rglob(` over tools/ and engine/src/); tools/README.md, "Year changes as operations".
- **Siblings checked:** Files under a year directory (tools/sources/2025.json and the like), the year-change tools themselves and tools/year_free_names.json are not scanned: they are per year, or name ids only as examples or as history. fixtures/<year> is carried by tools/fixtures_year.py, which already marks cases stating a removed input "not evaluated"; interview/<year> is covered by year_changes.py's dangling rule. A parameter that no line reads after the operations (O3a's f5695.rce_rate and the other Part II maxima, C-CRED-09) is a different gap and is not listed here. The New York jurisdiction uses the same scan (`--jurisdiction ny`; no New York operations exist).
- **Regression predictions:** No value changes; the tool writes reports and a note. `year_changes.py --check` prints one more note when the operations remove a referenced id (none in this tree's changes/2026; 412 references once O5's and O3a's files merge). `tools/self_tests.py` runs one more self-test, `year_shared_refs_self_test`, which plants an id, a longer id that is not a reference, an instance id, a templated local name, another form's same local name, an untemplated local name, a mutation key, a gate retired and a gate still used, and a per-year file. `tier_paths.py --self-test` still fails in the base on four entries that predate this lane (engine/src/draft-walk.ts, tick-groups-check.ts, tick-groups.ts, tools/ny_fixtures.py); the new tool is not among them.

## BUG-0645 — The adoption's year-literal list misses the neighbouring years (2024, 2026) a 2025 definition names

- **Date:** 2026-11-14.
- **Caught by:** lane O6 of the TY2026 preparation (claude-opus-5-5, judgment), writing the 2026 help of f8889.testing_prior (which names 2024 and 2023 for the prior years and $4,150 and $8,300 for the 2024 limits).
- **Source:** tools/year_diff.py year_literal(): a line is listed when it names the from-year or an id bearing a year; the prior year (2024 in a 2025 tree, to become 2025) and the next year (2026, to become 2027) are not looked for.
- **Symptom:** Measured on the worktree's forms/2025 and interview/2025 (a python pass with year_diff.year_literal): 588 lines outside locator/quote lines name 2024 or 2026; 373 of them are not flagged, so adopting 2026 copies them silently. Examples: person.yaml:3065 'Your distributions in 2023 and 2024 ... and in 2026', the f8889 prior-year questions ('during 2024', 'For 2024, was more put into your HSA'), the HSA testing-period help. The count over-states somewhat: a per-line test also misses continuation lines of a multi-line locator (sa.yaml:511 is one), which the same function treats as definitions.
- **Tags:** tool change, year rollover
- **Tool change:** Fixed in the adoption tooling by lane R6 (claude-opus-5-5, judgment), 2026-11-14. `tools/year_diff.py` lists every year a copied line names outside a citation, not only the from-year, and classes each one: `from_year`, `year_id` (an id or constant bearing a year; `amb.2025.x` now included, which the per-line test caught only as the bare from-year), `birth_cutoff` (BUG-0646), `adjacent_year` (three years before the from-year to two after: prior returns, carryovers, testing periods, the next year), `fixed_reference` (a document number such as Notice 2025-69 or Rev. Proc. 2024-40) and `other_year` (statutory and historical dates). A citation is now the whole `locator:` or `quote:` scalar with its continuation lines, so the 357 continuation lines that were listed as definitions (sa.yaml:511 is one) are no longer listed; every one of them was checked to sit inside a locator. A line whose moving years (the from-year, the adjacent years, the years of birth) can be shifted carries the shifted text as a `moved` candidate; nothing is edited, because an adjacent year can be a statutory date (carloan "originated after December 31, 2024" stays). The lines are scanned in the from-year files and reported at the same line of the copy, and a line the copy already converted (tax_year) is not listed. The JSON records are now objects (file, line, text, classes, age_params, moved), and the year-diff report groups them by class. Measured on this tree's 2025 forms, tables, parameters, register and interview: 2,875 lines listed (the earlier test listed 2,657, of which 357 were locator continuations); 510 lines name an adjacent year, 85 a year of birth, 88 a document number, 144 another year; 2,291 carry a moved candidate. Lane O6 moved the f8889.testing_prior and f8889.fsa help to 2026 in changes/2026/f8889.yaml (C-PRI-20); the prompts of f8889.ira_prior, f8889.testing_prior and the other prior-year questions are left for adoption, where they are now listed as `adjacent_year`.
- **Tool files:** tools/year_diff.py: new `YEAR_TEXT`, `BIRTH`, `KEY_LINE`, `CITATION_KEYS`, `LITERAL_CLASSES`, `birth_cutoffs`, `literal_scan`, `year_literal_report`, `self_test_literals`; `YEAR_ID` widened to `amb.2025.x`; `adopt` (its year-literal block only, now a call of `year_literal_report`); `write_report` (the year-literal section, grouped by class); `self_test` (the per-line literal check replaced by a call of `self_test_literals`); `year_literal` removed (its one caller was the literal block); module docstring. tools/README.md, "Year changes as operations".
- **Siblings checked:** The New York adoption (`--jurisdiction ny`) takes the same code; its parameters have no `age.*` values, so it gets every class but `birth_cutoff`. `tools/check_year_ids.py` (ids bearing a year in the build) is unchanged and still passes ("no new id carries a year"). The relocation of citations (`citations.py --relocate`) is what moves the skipped locator text; unchanged. The interview bank names no year of birth (grep over interview/2025). R2's carry functions and R3's `extend_year_enums`/`extend_recovery_year` in `adopt` are untouched.
- **Regression predictions:** No form, parameter or fixture value changes: the tool writes reports only. At the next adoption `reports/<to>/year_literals_from_<from>.json` changes shape (objects, not [file, line, text]) and holds more lines; nothing else reads it except `write_report`. `year_diff.py --self-test` gains one check (the classed list, with a copied tax_year, a locator continuation, adjacent years, years of birth, a fixed birth date, a year without a birth word, a document number, an id, a block scalar and the age parameters' own values planted) and drops the per-line check it replaces; a probe with the citation continuation rule disabled, and one with the birth rule disabled, each made it fail.

## BUG-0646 — Birth-date cutoffs one year off the tax year (January 2, 1961; December 31, 1960) in labels, sources and prompts are not moved or listed by adoption

- **Caught by:** lane O8 (TY2026 preparation, Schedule 1-A), 2026-11-14.
- **Symptom:** year_diff.py --adopt lists only literals naming the from-year (2025). Age cutoffs printed as the year minus 64 or minus 65 (January 2, 1961; born after December 31, 1960; January 2, 1960 on refund.yaml) appear in about 40 labels, input sources and citation locators of forms/2025 (person, sa, s3, household, eic, refund, s1a) and in bank prompts. Adoption neither moves them nor puts them on the worklist, so the 2026 tree would print 2025 cutoffs. Lane O8 moved the s1a labels by operation (C-SCHED-08); the others are unowned.
- **Where:** tools/year_diff.py year_literal(); forms/2025/{person,sa,s3,household,eic,refund}.yaml (grep '1961\|1960').
- **Remedy:** Extend the adoption literal list to the offset years D7 names for the age.* parameters (from-year minus 64, 65, and the EIC bounds), or move these labels by operations in the owning lanes.
- **Tags:** tool change, year rollover
- **Tool change:** Fixed in the adoption tooling by lane R6 (claude-opus-5-5, judgment), 2026-11-14, as a listed class, not as an automatic edit and not by generating the text from the parameters. `tools/year_diff.py` reads the year-moving parameters of the from-year (`birth_cutoffs`: a parameter that declares `moves_with_year: N`, as lane P2 adds on the 14 `age.*`; an `age.*` Count that declares nothing is taken to move by 1, so the rule holds on a tree without P2's flags). A year on a copied line outside a citation is classed `birth_cutoff` when it equals such a parameter's value or the year before it (born before January 2, 1961 is `age.cut_65`; born after December 31, 1960 is the year before it) and a word of birth (born, birth, birthday) stands on its line or the line before it in the same scalar. The record names the parameters it sits beside and carries the line with the year moved by the year step as a candidate. A parameter whose value sits at the tax year (`age.birth_year_latest`) is not a cut-off. The age parameters' own `value:` lines are classed the same way (propose_params.py moves them). Measured on this tree: 85 lines, 65 of them in forms (person 33, s1a 16, refund 7, s3 3, sa 2, f8880 2, eic 1, f8889 1), 13 parameter values and 7 register lines; every line of forms/2025 that names 1960 or 1961 outside a citation is among them. Years of birth that are fixed by statute stay out of the class: Form 4972's "born before January 2, 1936" (retirement.yaml) and the 2001 election and "gift after 1976" in sales.yaml (1976 is `age.cut_50`'s value but has no birth word) are `other_year`.
  Why not generate the text from the parameter: no label, source, help or bank prompt is templated today, so it would add interpolation to the build, the renderer and the interview runtime, and the transcription and render reviews compare these labels literally with the printed form text (s1a line 36a, s3 and sa labels quote the form). That cost recurs for about 65 lines that the classed list now hands the adoption lane with the parameter named and the moved text ready. Why not move them automatically: the same years appear as fixed dates (1936, the 2001 election, a 1976 gift, September 11, 2001), and a rule that edits would have to be right about each; a listed candidate costs a reading.
- **Tool files:** tools/year_diff.py `birth_cutoffs`, `literal_scan` (the `birth_cutoff` class), `year_literal_report` (`age_params`, `moved`), `self_test_literals`; tools/README.md, "Year changes as operations".
- **Siblings checked:** All 14 `age.*` parameters of params/2025.yaml (each matched by value or the year before it; the 13 cut-offs and `age.birth_year_earliest` value lines are classed `birth_cutoff`, `age.birth_year_latest` sits at the tax year and is excluded). The interview bank (no year of birth in a prompt, by grep). The register (`ambiguities/2025.yaml`, 7 lines listed). f8880's "born after January 1, 2008" (`age.cut_18`) and f8889's "born in 1970 or earlier; ... born in 1971" (`age.cut_55`; the 1971 occurrence is the cut-off itself and is moved too). The s1a labels lane O8 moved by operation (C-SCHED-08) are still listed: `adopt` makes the list before it applies the operations (an order this fix keeps), so those entries show the from-year text and the copy then holds the operations' text; the line numbers are those of the copy before the operations.
- **Regression predictions:** No value changes; the tool writes reports only. At the next adoption the year-literal list gains a `birth_cutoff` section (about 85 lines from the 2025 tree). The self-test plants a cut-off year (born before January 2, 1961), the year before one (born after December 31, 1960), a continuation line whose birth word is on the line before, a block-scalar line, a fixed birth date (1936), a cut-off value without a birth word (a gift after 1976) and the parameters' own values; disabling the birth rule made it fail.

## BUG-0647 — The 2026 Tax Computation Worksheet for joint filers needs a 12% row the 2025 worksheet lacks

- **Date:** 2026-11-14.
- **Caught by:** lane P2 (claude-opus-5-5, judgment), deriving the 2026 Tax Computation Worksheet rows from the rate tables (plan decision D8) in tools/propose_params.py, which compares the rows over the Tax Table boundary in each year.
- **Source:** rp-25-32 p. 10, section 4.01, Table 1 (married filing jointly and surviving spouses): the 12% bracket runs to $100,800 ("Over $24,800 but not over $100,800", "plus 12% of the excess over $24,800"); the 2025 table (rp-2024-40) ended it at $96,950.
- **Symptom:** forms/2025/tcw.yaml section B (married filing jointly, qualifying surviving spouse) has five rows, the first at 22% from ordinary.table_boundary ($100,000). In 2026 the income from $100,000 to $100,800 is in the 12% bracket, so carried as is, row 1 at 22% would compute the tax on $100,000 to $100,800 too low (by 10% of the distance to $100,800: $80 at $100,000, $30 at $100,500). Single, separate and head-of-household sections are unaffected (their 22% brackets start below $100,000). The change map (research/ty2026/changes.md) has no entry for it; it is found from the revenue procedure, before the 2026 Form 1040 instructions print the worksheet.
- **Tags:** year change, tax computation, TY2026
- **Year change:** Fixed as a 2026 year-change operation, `changes/2026/tcw.yaml` (form tcw, change BUG-0647, verified: final, evidence rp-25-32 p. 10 "Over $24,800 but not over $100,800" and "$2,480 plus 12% of the excess over $24,800"). It adds Section B row 0 (`mfj.row0.product` = amount x tcw.mfj.b0.rate; `mfj.row0.tax` = product less tcw.mfj.b0.subtract), cited to rp-25-32 p. 10 until the 2026 Form 1040 instructions print the worksheet. `mfj.result`'s choose gains a first alternative (amount at least ordinary.table_boundary and not over tcw.mfj.b0.upper: row 0), and row 1's guard starts over tcw.mfj.b0.upper instead of at the boundary. The new ids are row0 and b0, so rows 1 to 5 and their parameters keep their ids. Whether the 2026 worksheet prints the row as row 1 is checked when i1040gi 2026 posts, with the relocation of the worksheet's i1040gi cites. The three parameters are staged in research/ty2026/params-2026.proposed.yaml: tcw.mfj.b0.upper $100,800, .rate 12/100, .subtract $496. The subtraction amount is from the D8 rule of tools/propose_params.py (rate x lower limit less base: 12% x $24,800 - $2,480), and that rule now numbers a status's rows from its lowest (b0 or b1), so the 2026 to 2027 proposal derives the new row too (self-test case added).
- **Year change lines:** `tcw.mfj.row0.product`, `tcw.mfj.row0.tax` (new, 2026), `tcw.mfj.result` (expr.alternatives), and parameters `tcw.mfj.b0.upper`, `tcw.mfj.b0.rate`, `tcw.mfj.b0.subtract` (staged 2026).
- **Siblings checked:** the other 2026 sections, by the 2026 schedule's first row over the boundary: Section A single (12% ends $50,400, so the 22% row covers $100,000), Section C married filing separately ($50,400), and Section D head of household ($67,450) need no row, so they are left as they are. The top rows and the remaining Section B rows: their 2026 values all equal the rate-table rows (extract_printed_tables.rate_schedule check on the staged values: the 20 worksheet rows agree). The callers of the definition: `tax_on_amount` (forms/2025/tax_on_amount.yaml), used by f1040.line16, the qdcg worksheet and the sdtw worksheet. All of them reach the new row through tcw.mfj.result with no change of their own. The Tax Table below $100,000 is read from tables/<year>/tax_table and is untouched.
- **Regression predictions:** 2025 is unchanged, because the operation applies only to 2026. In a scratch tree, with the operation written by year_changes.write and Section B's parameters set to the staged 2026 values, `build` gave build OK. Five joint returns, with line 15 at $100,000, $100,500, $100,800, $100,801 and $100,900, gave line 16 of $11,504.00, $11,564.00, $11,600.00, $11,600.22 and $11,622.00. Each is equal to the 2026 rate table, and the prediction was made from the table before running. Without the row, the first three would be $80, $30 and $0 lower. The 2025 fixtures have no joint case with line 15 from $100,000 to $100,800 (the one case at $100,000, qdcg switch.exact, is single), and research/ty2026/fixtures-proposed has no tcw case, so no predicted 2026 case changes.

## BUG-0648 — A render log with no line subjects stays stale after year_carry carries every line: the rendered header names the tax year

- **Date:** 2026-11-14.
- **Caught by:** lane R2 of the TY2026 preparation (claude-opus-5-5, judgment), in a scratch rehearsal adopting the 2025 documents as 2026 (/tmp/ty26-r2-reh).
- **Symptom:** After year_diff.py --adopt, build, render and year_carry.py --write, check_logs.py --year 2026 reports for 11 forms (aqee, clcw, dcprov, f4562, f5329, f8606, interest, mq, se, tax_on_amount, tcw) 'the render log reviewed an earlier rendered English of <form>; rerun the review', though year_carry carried every compared line. Their 2025 render indexes have no line subjects (subjects is null), so subjects.index_state compares the whole rendered subject, and the only difference between rendered/2025/<form>.md and rendered/2026/<form>.md is the header line 'Document: <form> (def, tax year 2025)' vs '2026' (checked for tcw with the year masked: no other difference). The same holds at a real adoption, so these 11 render reviews would be paid again for a year mark.
- **Tags:** tool change, adoption, year carry, review store
- **Tool change:** `year_carry.py --write` now records a year-carried whole-form subject (`subject_carried`, `carried: {by: year, from}`) for a render index with no line subjects when every compared line carries, the TY index answered the TY rendering, and the two renderings (citations left out, as `subjects.of_rendered`) are equal once a year is normalized in lockstep where the document's cited sources moved it (`project_pair` with the shift evidence of the document's cited sections, the rule `rest_carries` applies to a transcription document's own fields). `review_store.recorded_subject` already reads `subject_carried`; `review_store.check` now accepts it from a year carry as well as a rename. A rendering that differs in anything but a moved year, or whose sources moved no year, or kept the year in the same words, still makes the log stale. The document's own tax year, which adoption writes (the rendered header `- Document: `<id>` (<kind>, tax year N)` and the `tax_year` field of a transcription document's own fields, `__rest__`), is normalized without source evidence, from TY to TY+1 only (`own_year`; coordinator decision under the owner's delegation, 2026-11-14: it is not content a reviewer judged against the IRS text); every other year, in line text, labels, citations or notes, still needs the sources to move it.
- **Tool files:** `tools/transcription/year_carry.py` (`OWN_YEAR`, `own_year`, `whole_carried`, `renderings_carry`, `rest_carries`, `write`, `self_test`), `tools/transcription/review_store.py` (`check`'s `subject_carried` test, `recorded_subject` docstring, module docstring).
- **Siblings checked:** the 62 transcription indexes of 2025 all have line subjects, so their own fields go through `__rest__` and `rest_carries`, which already normalizes `tax_year` by the same evidence rule; the 55 class M indexes have no line subjects but `subjects.of_computation` leaves out `tax_year` (rows of id, type, expr), and the rehearsal showed no class M log stale in 2026 that was current in 2025; New York's render logs showed no 2026-only render staleness in the rehearsal; the rename carry (`test_rename_carry.py`) still passes with the widened `subject_carried` check.
- **Regression predictions:** `year_carry.py --self-test`: a rendering whose header year moved where the sources moved the year carries; the same with no year moved in the sources, with the year kept in the same words, or with a sentence also changed does not; only the header's or the own `tax_year` moved by one carries with sources printing no year, moved by two or together with any other change does not. In the rehearsal (2025 documents adopted as 2026, sources unchanged, so no year moved in any source), `check_logs.py --year 2026` reports no render log stale for its whole rendering (the 11 forms before: aqee, clcw, dcprov, f4562, f5329, f8606, interest, mq, se, tax_on_amount, tcw) and no transcription log stale 'outside every compared line' (every form before); what stays stale is the carry's own verdict (ltc 2(b) and two person lines, enums ltc_age and person_role whose values changed) or stale in 2025 already (scope). `review_store.py check` passes on 2025 (315 indexes) and on the rehearsal's 2026.

## BUG-0649 — year_changes write drops a YAML anchor whose alias lives in an untouched block

- **Caught by:** lane O2 (TY2026 preparation), 2026-11-14, a scratch write of one operation.
- **Symptom:** tools/year_changes.py write_state redumps a changed line block from data, without its anchor. forms/2025/retirement.yaml has retirement.taxable refuses: &id002 and retirement.amount_a refuses: *id002. A single set on retirement.taxable, written into a scratch copy, leaves the adopted file unparseable: found undefined alias id002. A year_diff.py --adopt with such an operation would write a broken form.
- **Workaround:** An operation set changing the anchored block also sets every block that aliases it (lane O2's retirement.yaml entries set the refuses of retirement.taxable and retirement.amount_a together; that scratch write parses).
- **Proposed fix:** Either resolve anchors in forms (no aliases in form files, with a check) or have write_state rewrite every block holding an alias of a changed block, and plant the case in --self-test.
- **Tool change:** fixed by 2026 lane R3 (docs/provisional/lanes/ty26-r3.md): when a line is rewritten, `tools/year_changes.py` rewrites any kept line that aliases one of its anchors with the alias expanded, and the writer emits no anchors; `year_changes.py --self-test` plants this case (it fails with the fix switched off, "found undefined alias").
- **Tags:** tool change, year changes

## BUG-0650 — Year operations cannot edit the interview files a removal leaves naming removed ids (targets, personas, coverage rows, gate frequencies, bank groups)

- **Date:** 2026-11-14.
- **Caught by:** lane O3a of the TY2026 preparation (claude-opus-5-5, judgment), writing changes/2026/f5695.yaml (C-CRED-01 to -08).
- **Symptom:** The Form 5695 operations remove 217 lines and their bank questions. year_changes.py --check then fails 79 times with 'dangling: interview/<file> still names the removed <id>': interview/2025/full.yaml (target f5695.line32b), gate_frequencies.yaml (refs f5695.any in home_energy, clean_energy_part1, home_improvement_part2), personas/10_homeowner_solar_heat_pump.yaml (a persona of 2025 installations), and 20 rows of coverage/education_energy.yaml (l8b.energy_*). No operation kind edits these files: profiles' question lists are edited by add/remove_question, nothing else in interview/<year>/ is. The bank's group list is not editable either: the build of the applied tree fails 'group energy_power/energy_shell/energy_heating: no question names it'. The check's rule is right (these names would dangle in 2026); the operations cannot satisfy it.

- **Fix (proposed):** Add operation kinds for interview files keyed by file and path (for example remove_interview_file {file}, set_interview {file, field, from, to} with list values replaced whole, and an operation on the bank's groups), written block by block at adoption as the bank is; or decide that such files are edited by hand at adoption and make the check report (not fail) names in non-profile interview files. Either is an owner or tool-lane decision; the interview construction protocol applies to whatever replaces the energy persona and coverage rows.

## BUG-0651 — TY2026 operations ask for the Form 1062 farmland installment election twice

- **Date:** 2026-11-14.
- **Caught by:** lane O3b (claude-opus-5-5, judgment) while writing changes/2026/s3.yaml (C-SCHED-39); read from the operations and the 2025 forms, not from a run of an applied interview.
- **Source:** f1040s3 (2026 draft) p. 2, line 13e, "Total section 1062 applicable net tax liability. Enter amount from Form 1062, line 14"; f1040 (2026 draft) p. 3, line 24b, "Enter amount from Form 1062, line 15".
- **Symptom:** changes/2026/f1040.yaml (C-PRI-04) adds the input f1040.form1062 ("Are you electing to pay the tax on gain from a sale or exchange of qualified farmland property to a qualified farmer in four annual installments (Form 1062)?"), refused on f1040.line24b. forms/2025/s3.yaml already asks for the same section 1062 election through s3.farmland and s3.farmland_deferral (refused on s3.line14, which changes/2026/s3.yaml now cites to Schedule 3 line 13e). Applied to 2026, a filer who sold farmland is asked about the one election twice, by two questions worded differently, and either refuses. f1040.form1062 also has no parent (bank order 20) and is read by f1040.line24b, which feeds line 24c, so every filer would have been asked it; the 2025 design asks about the election only beneath a tick box. This is inferred from the operations, not from a walk.
- **Tags:** year change, interview, TY2026 operations
- **Fix:** The election is asked once, by the existing Schedule 3 pair. Under the interview construction protocol that pair is already the cheaper walk: s3.farmland is the "Sold farmland" box of the rare_credits tick-box screen (N12), and s3.farmland_deferral is asked only beneath it (N2, N8). The filer with no farmland sale unticks one box. f1040.form1062 was a 20-plus-word election question every filer had to read and answer No to (N4, N8). In changes/2026/f1040.yaml (C-PRI-04), the add_line and add_question of f1040.form1062 are removed. f1040.line24b is added after f1040.line24 and refuses on s3.farmland_deferral_if_sold. The 2026 sources put the election on two lines, Form 1040 line 24b (Form 1062 line 15, the first installment) and Schedule 3 line 13e (Form 1062 line 14), so the same gate now refuses on both: f1040.line24b, and s3.line14, inside which line 13e stays. In changes/2026/s3.yaml (C-SCHED-39), s3.farmland_deferral's label and source are reworded to the 2026 election ("choose to pay the tax on the gain from a sale or exchange of qualified farmland property to a qualified farmer in installments (Form 1062)"), its question prompt being unchanged. It and s3.farmland_deferral_if_sold now cite i1062 p. 2 (2026 draft), What's New, instead of the 2025 i1040gi line 13z sentence. A new split file, changes/2026/scope.credits.yaml (C-SCHED-39), gives scope.ready_credits' refusal on the same gate the line 13e wording and citation of s3.line14's. The question bank is unchanged.
- **Fix lines:** `f1040.line24b`, `s3.farmland_deferral`, `s3.farmland_deferral_if_sold`, `s3.line14`, `scope.ready_credits`; removed from the 2026 operations: `f1040.form1062` and its bank entry.

## BUG-0652 — Adoption does not carry reviews/<year>/twins.json, which the twin check requires for the new year

- **Date:** 2026-11-14.
- **Caught by:** lane O5 of the TY2026 preparation (claude-opus-5-5, judgment), checking that its Part III operations keep the person and dependent sides in step.
- **Symptom:** tools/check_twins.py exits with 'reviews/<year>/twins.json is missing' for a year without one; year_diff.py --adopt copies reviews/<from>/citations.json but not twins.json (grep: only check_twins.py and siblings.py name the file), so the twins step of check-all would fail on the first run for 2026. The 2026 Part III operations also change declared values (the year in labels, prompts and questions; the TIN lines removed), so a plain copy would fail too: applied in a scratch copy, check_twins reports 18 problems, all restatements of declared differences except one intended new difference (edu_student_tin's guard: household.any_work_ssn against dependent.work_ssn_known).
- **Tool change:** in part, by lane R2: `year_diff.py --adopt` carries `reviews/<year>/twins.json`. Open: restating the declared differences that the 2026 operations change (T-327).
- **Tags:** tool change, adoption, twins
- **Fix (proposed):** Have --adopt copy reviews/<from>/twins.json to the new year, and add an operation kind (or a carried step after the operations apply) that restates declared values the operations changed; until then the adoption lane rewrites reviews/2026/twins.json from the problems check_twins.py lists.

## BUG-0653 — Writing year operations drops a YAML anchor that an untouched block aliases

- **Date:** 2026-11-14.
- **Caught by:** lane O6 of the TY2026 preparation (claude-opus-5-5, judgment), probing tools/year_changes.py write() before setting a field of f8962.line24.
- **Source:** tools/year_changes.py, rewrite_list and item_text (a changed block is re-dumped with yaml.dump, which writes resolved data and no anchors).
- **Symptom:** forms/2025/f8962.yaml line f8962.line24 holds 'refuses: &id003', which f8962.line25 aliases ('refuses: *id003'). In a scratch copy (/tmp/o6/anchor: forms/2025, interview/2025, params/2025.yaml copied from the worktree) one operation setting f8962.line24's label, written by year_changes.write(2025, 2026, root=scratch), left a file that does not load: 'found undefined alias' at line 2842 (line 25's refuses). year_changes.py --check applies in memory and passes, and --self-test plants no anchors, so the defect would first show at year_diff.py --adopt, after the copy. Anchors that later blocks alias in forms/2025: f8962.yaml &alloc_cite, &other_cite, &adjust_cite, &id001, &id002, &id003; f1095a.yaml &id001, &id005 and others (grep '&' forms/2025).
- **Duplicate of:** BUG-0649 (the same anchor defect of the adoption writer, found from f8962.line24).
- **Tool change:** fixed with BUG-0649 by lane R3.
- **Tags:** tool change, year operations
- **Proposed fix:** Not fixed (lane O6 owns no tool). Candidates: refuse in --check an operation that changes a block defining an anchor some untouched block aliases (cheap; names the lines), or have write() expand the alias in every aliasing block it must then rewrite, or remove anchors from forms (the build reads data, not anchors). Lane O6 worked round it: C-PEOP-27 does not extend the remedy text of f8962.line24's refusal list.
- **Proposed fix lines:** none

## BUG-0654 — The Schedule C material-participation question also admits the oil and gas working-interest exception, which the 2026 minimum QBI deduction does not

- **Caught by:** lane ty26-o7 (TY2026 year-change operations for C-SCHED-31), 2026-11-14.
- **Source:** plaw-119-21 p. 92, section 199A(i)(2)(B), an active qualified trade or business is one "in which the taxpayer materially participates (within the meaning of section 469(h))"; i8995 (2026 draft) p. 6, Line 17, "with respect to all qualified trades or businesses in which you materially participated for the taxable year, within the meaning of section 469(h)".
- **Symptom:** sc.passive (Schedule C line G) is answered Yes both for material participation and for a directly held working interest in an oil or gas well (the section 469(c)(3) exception, which is not material participation). The 2026 operations (changes/2026/f8995.yaml, f8995.min_qualifies) count every Schedule C business on a completed return as active, so a working interest held without material participation would count toward the $1,000 of active qualified business income. The case is believed empty on a completed return because such an interest claims depletion and depletion (line 12) is refused by the Schedule C screen, but that rests on the filer claiming depletion, not on a check.
- **Where:** forms/2025/sc.yaml sc.passive and its bank question; changes/2026/f8995.yaml C-SCHED-31 (f8995.min_qualifies).
- **Proposed fix:** At the 2026 adoption, either ask the oil and gas exception as its own Yes (beneath line G, refusing it, or excluding that business from f8995.min_qualifies), or record the depletion argument as the reason in the line's citation; owner's choice.
- **Tags:** QBI; year 2026; low

## BUG-0655 — Home storage space counted without the sole-fixed-location test

- **Date:** 2026-11-14.
- **Caught by:** lane O9 of the TY2026 preparation (claude-opus-5-5, judgment), writing the operations of C-BUS-06.
- **Source:** p587 (2025) p. 3, Storage of inventory or product samples, "Your home is the only fixed location of your trade or business" (one of the tests that must all be met); i1040sc (2026, draft) p. 11, Simplified method, "Space used for storage is allowed only if the residence is the sole fixed location of your business".
- **Symptom:** sc.ho_uses and sc.ho_sqft (forms/2025/sc.yaml) count space used regularly for storing inventory or product samples with no condition; a filer who stores stock at home but has another fixed place of business gets a simplified-method deduction for that space, which Pub. 587 does not allow. The 2025 i1040sc does not state the test; the 2025 p587, which sc.ho_uses refers to, does.
- **Tags:** sc, home office, 2025 definitions
- **Proposed fix:** For 2026 the condition is written as operations (changes/2026/sc.yaml, C-BUS-06: the source of sc.ho_uses and sc.ho_sqft, the question of sc.ho_uses and a help on sc.ho_sqft). Whether 2025 is mended is the owner's or the 2025 lane's decision (the 2025 tree is frozen for its landing; D12).
- **Proposed fix lines:** sc.ho_uses, sc.ho_sqft (2025, open)

## BUG-0678 — BUG-0443 and BUG-0453 are fixed: the Form 8889 questions name the HSA-only medical costs, the family-plan deductible test, cash-only deposits and insurer contributions; the line 15 item is unreachable

- **Date:** 2026-11-15

## BUG-0689 — A person on a Marketplace plan someone else signed up for, with no Form 1095-A of their own, is asked nothing about Form 8962

- **Date:** 2026-11-15
- **Caught by:** redraft lane l8a (docs/provisional/lanes/l8a.md, "Found and not fixed"), carried in TASKS.md T-310 (l8a); recorded and fixed by lane g1-f3.
- **Source:** i8962 (2025) p. 12, Allocating policy amounts, "The other tax family received a Form 1095-A for the policy that includes a member of your tax family" and "You or an individual in your tax family was enrolled in a qualified health plan by someone who is not part of your tax family (for example, your ex-spouse enrolled a child whom you are claiming as a dependent)"; f1095a p. 3, Instructions for Recipient, "If you or your family members enrolled at the Marketplace in more than one qualified health plan policy, you will receive a Form 1095-A for each policy."
- **Symptom:** the roster question `$f1095a` ("did you ..., or anyone you claim as a dependent, have health insurance bought through HealthCare.gov or a state Marketplace?") offers only "No" and "Yes, with N Forms 1095-A", and its help said each form is "kept in your online account". A filer covered by a plan someone else signed up for, whose form went to that person, has no form of their own and may answer No. Nothing about Form 8962 is then asked: a plan shared with another tax family is not refused (Part IV), and a plan that covered only people on this return is left off Form 8962 although it must be reconciled. A missing form or a missing refusal.
- **Where:** interview/2025/questions.yaml, the `$f1095a` entry (help).
- **Status:** fixed in the bank only; no form line changed, so the entry names no Fix lines. The help now reads: "Each plan has its own Form 1095-A. Count a plan someone else signed up for too, even if its form went to them (ask them for a copy). Count a corrected form in place of the one it replaces, not a VOID one. With only a catastrophic or dental plan, answer No." The filer who counts such a plan reaches the Marketplace people screen (order 196) before any form entry. If the plan also covered someone not on the return, the box `f8962.shared_policy` ("The plan also covered someone who is not on this return"; its help already says "Count a plan whose Form 1095-A went to someone else") refuses through `f8962.alloc` as before. If the plan covered only people on the return, the copy is entered and the credit reconciled as for the filer's own form, which is what the instructions require. The l8a alternative, a second question after a No, was not built: it is a guard asked after the typical answer (protocol N4), and the prompt already asks the right fact. No step or prompt word is added for any filer; the help went from 43 to 52 words, over the protocol's 40 (N10), as the old help already was. A filer who does not open the help can still answer No wrongly. That is the remaining risk, for the question review to judge.
- **Regression predictions:** help only; no value, refusal or walk changes.
- **Tags:** interview; Form 8962; help; low

## BUG-0690 — BUG-0504's fix sketch would expose the unmodeled year-of-marriage column (b) and line 10 rules: the Table 4 narrowing is not safe alone

- **Date:** 2026-11-15
- **Caught by:** lane g1-f3, checking BUG-0504 against the tree and i8962 before fixing it.
- **Source:** i8962 (2025) p. 13, Table 4, questions 1 to 5; p. 17, Column (b), "Marriage in 2025. If you got married in 2025, and someone in your tax family who you enrolled in a qualified health plan (including yourself) and someone in your tax family who your spouse enrolled in a qualified health plan (including your spouse) prior to your first month of marriage receives separate Forms 1095-A, add together the amounts from column B of the Forms 1095-A for each month before the first full month of marriage and enter the total."; p. 22, Line 34, "If you got married in 2025 and APTC was paid for an individual in your tax family, see Table 4 ... If you do not complete Part V, check “No” on Form 8962, line 10; skip line 11".
- **Symptom:** BUG-0504 is real as recorded: `f8962.married_this_year` (the entry's `married_in_2025`, renamed by the redraft) refuses every joint return with Marketplace coverage before the first full month of a 2025 marriage, including filers that Table 4 makes ineligible for Part V. Its fix sketch, which narrows the question to Table 4's conditions, is not safe as written. The refusal is the only guard for two more year-of-marriage rules the tool does not model. (1) The p. 17 column (b) rule: each spouse's separate pre-marriage forms are added for the months before the first full month of marriage. `f1095a.b_counted` tells a filer to count only one form from the same state for a shared month, so it would be wrong for them. (2) The p. 22 sentence: line 10 is No when APTC was paid and Part V is not completed. `f8962.line10` does not read the marriage. The refusal's remedy already says "the year-of-marriage rules (Part V and Pub. 974)". Narrowing by Table 4 questions 1 and 5 alone would let both cases reach a completed return. Over-refusal stays the current behaviour; no value is wrong today.
- **Where:** forms/2025/f8962.yaml, `f8962.married_this_year`, `f8962.marriage`, `f8962.line10`; forms/2025/f1095a.yaml, `f1095a.b_counted`.
- **Proposed fix:** for the owner, not built. (a) Keep the refusal. (b) A narrow safe release: no refusal when the couple's only pre-marriage coverage is on one Form 1095-A and no advance payments were made on any form (Table 4 question 5 No). This is derivable from line 33C and the roster with no new question, but the refusal would then be told only after the forms are entered (N11). (c) The full release (no APTC, no excess APTC, or not unmarried on January 1) needs the p. 17 column (b) rule in `b_counted` and the p. 22 line 10 rule as new arithmetic. Reach is small in all three: couples married in 2025 with Marketplace coverage before the marriage.
- **Tags:** Form 8962; refusal; year of marriage; correction; low; open

## BUG-0692 — BUG-0593 is fixed: refunds of both spouses' tax on separate 2024 returns are asked about and refused or zero

- **Date:** 2026-11-15
- **Closes:** BUG-0593
- **Caught by:** BUG-0593, recorded open; this entry closes it because the inventory is append-only.
- **Source:** i1040gi p. 88, Line 1, TIP, "None of your refund is taxable if, in the year you paid the tax, you either (a) didn’t itemize deductions, or (b) elected to deduct state and local general sales taxes"; p. 89, Exception, items 1 to 9 (none names the case); p. 90, State and Local Income Tax Refund Worksheet, lines 1, 2, 4 and 5 (one 2024 return); p525 p. 24, Itemized Deduction Recoveries.
- **Symptom:** as recorded in BUG-0593.
- **Fix:** on a joint 2025 return, refund.two_returns asks "Were these refunds for 2024 tax of both of you, when each of you filed your own 2024 federal return (for example, before you married, or as married filing separately)?" (help: if only one of you got a refund, answer No; the 2024 questions are then about that person's own return). On Yes, refund.two_itemized asks "Did either of you itemize deductions on your own 2024 federal return and deduct state and local income taxes there (not general sales taxes)?". No: refund.worksheet is false and none of the refund is taxable (the TIP holds for both returns). Yes: refund.taxable refuses on refund.two_itemized_if_two (Pub. 525, Itemized Deduction Recoveries (Worksheet 2)). The per-spouse worksheet was not built: the instructions do not print it. Reading recorded as amb.2025.refund_two_returns, for the owner's review.
- **Fix lines:** `refund.two_returns`, `refund.two_returns_if_joint`, `refund.two_itemized`, `refund.two_itemized_if_two`, `refund.joint`, `refund.no`, `refund.worksheet`, `refund.worksheet_one`, `refund.taxable`
- **Siblings checked:** `refund.itemized`, `refund.sales`, `refund.line5d_prior_year`, `refund.line5e_prior_year`, `refund.line17_prior_year`, `refund.status`, `refund.spouse_born`, `refund.spouse_blind`, `refund.mfs_spouse_itemized` (the one-return questions; on a joint return with one spouse's refund they now refer to that spouse's return through the help of refund.two_returns; no wording change), `refund.exc_who` (item 9, a different case: a joint state return with a person not on the 2025 return; unchanged), `refund.received_if_worksheet`, `refund.line1` to `refund.line9` (read refund.worksheet through the same choose; unchanged), `s1.line1` (reads refund.taxable; unchanged); the lines changed here, among them `refund.two_returns_if_joint` and `refund.two_itemized_if_two`.
- **Regression predictions:** no recorded value changes: every existing case that reads the worksheet is single, or joint with one 2024 return, and answers refund.two_returns No (the new default; stated in classm.refund.3, whose inputs are listed in full). New cases g1f4.refund.two_returns_standard (taxable 0) and g1f4.refuse.refund.two_itemized (refused), predicted by hand; coverage rows home.refund_two_returns_standard, home.refund_two_returns_itemized, home.refund_couple_one_return.

## BUG-0699 — BUG-0529 is fixed: Schedule C expense and cost of goods sold question lows

- **Date:** 2026-11-15
- **Closes:** BUG-0529
- **Caught by:** BUG-0529, recorded open from the question review of 2026-11-10 (reviews/2025/questions/sc.json, read finding by finding against the bank as it now stands after the interview redraft); goal-1 lane g1-f5 (claude-opus-5-5, judgment).
- **Source:** i1040sc pp. 6-10 and 15, the cited line instructions: p. 6, Line 2, "A sales allowance is a reduction in the selling price of products, instead of a cash or credit refund"; p. 8, Line 15, "Deduct on line 14 amounts paid for employee accident and health insurance"; p. 8, Line 17, "Also, include expenses incurred in resolving asserted tax deficiencies related to your business"; p. 8, Line 19, "This deduction may be subject to limitations"; p. 8, Line 18, "office supplies and postage"; p. 9, Line 22, "unless you deducted them in a prior tax year"; p. 9, Line 23, "Taxes assessed to pay for improvements, such as paving and sewers"; f1040sc p. 2, lines 33 and 35 to 41.
- **Symptom:** as recorded in BUG-0529.
- **Fix:** wording, in the bank (help, one line each): `sc.line2` (refunds and price cuts given after a sale; not discounts already off the price, nor refunds of money not counted as income), `sc.line15` (employees' health insurance goes with their benefits), `sc.line17` (include settling a tax dispute about the business; leave out fees for buying property or starting the business), `sc.line19` (only the deductible amount, within the plan's limits), `sc.line22` (leave out office supplies and postage, asked before, and supplies deducted in an earlier year), `sc.line23` (leave out charges for improvements such as paving or sewers), `sc.line39` (leave out what lines 35 to 38 and Part II already hold), `sc.line41` (value at cost, not at selling price). Already met by the redraft's prompts, so closed without a change: `sc.line8`, `sc.line10`, `sc.line36` (no year: each prompt now says "in 2025"), `sc.line11` (its help's list is open, "such as"), `sc.line24a` (the bare lodging-taxes bullet is no longer in the prompt or help), `sc.meals_100` (the prompt asks for food and drink, so a party's entertainment is not asked). Closed as not reached: `sc.line10` sale commissions to capitalize (a sale of business property is refused, `sd.business_property`), `sc.line35` and every fiscal-year reading (no fiscal-year filer is in scope; nothing in the 2025 forms or bank provides for one), `sc.line6` finance reserve income (a dealer's financing reserve; adding the term would put jargon in the help of every business, N6 and N10), `sc.line16b` capitalized interest (the producers who must capitalize interest are refused by `sc.method_other`, uniform capitalization).
- **Fix lines:** `sc.line2`, `sc.line15`, `sc.line17`, `sc.line19`, `sc.line22`, `sc.line23`, `sc.line39`, `sc.line41` (bank help only)
- **Siblings checked:** `sc.line3`, `sc.line28`, `sc.line28_pre179`, `sc.line14`, `sc.line18`, `sc.line19_if_employees`, `sc.line35`, `sc.line36`, `sc.line37`, `sc.line38`, `sc.line39_if_goods`, `sc.line41_if_goods`, `sc.line16a`, `sc.line16b`, `sc.line20b`, `sc.line21`, `sc.line25`, `sc.line6`, `sc.special` (readers and anchors of the changed questions; no expression changes, wording unchanged except as listed). The fix's own lines: `sc.line2`, `sc.line15`, `sc.line17`, `sc.line19`, `sc.line22`, `sc.line23`, `sc.line39`, `sc.line41`.

Met by the redraft and closed without a change: `sc.special` chapter 11 (the item moved to `scope.chapter11`, which asks whether the filer was in such a case in 2025), `sc.spouse_owned` de facto partnership (the prompt now asks plainly whether the business is owned with the husband or wife). Left open: `sc.at_risk` qualified nonrecourse financing on real property, `sc.passive` rental exceptions, `sc.tips_ot` a loss business (all three over-refusals: the return is refused, never wrong), and `sc.method_other` short-history gross receipts above $31 million.

The fix's own lines: `sc.passive`, `sc.method_other`, `sc.statutory`, `sc.ho_uses`, `sc.special`.
- **Regression predictions:** no existing value changes (no fixture or coverage row turns on a change of method in 2022 to 2024 or on a non-exclusive daycare). ## BUG-0711 — BUG-0506 is fixed: the charitable property screen measures $5,000 on the deduction, and restricted securities are not publicly traded

- **Date:** 2026-11-15
- **Closes:** BUG-0506
- **Caught by:** BUG-0506, recorded open; this entry closes it because the inventory is append-only (lane g1-f6, claude-opus-5-5, judgment).
- **Source:** i8283 p. 1, "Make any required reductions to the amount of the contributions before you determine if you must file Form 8283"; i8283 p. 3, Section B, "for which you claimed a deduction of more than $5,000"; Treas. Reg. 1.170A-13(c)(1)(i) and (c)(7)(xi)(B), (C) (cfr-26-1-170a-13, archived by this lane).
- **Symptom:** as recorded in BUG-0506.
- **Fix:** wording. (1) The first item of `gift.special` ("worth more than $5,000 in all, or your deduction for it is more than $5,000, and it is not publicly traded securities") is removed from the prompt, label and source: the deduction test is already made by `gift.section_b` from `gift.deduction`, and the regulation measures the threshold on "the amount claimed or reported as a deduction". Property worth more than $5,000 whose reduced deduction is $5,000 or less is now computed (Section A). i8283 p. 3 also says "A separate, qualified appraisal is required for any gift of property valued in excess of $5,000"; the regulation is followed over that sentence. (2) Section A item 2.d securities are not named, by decision: the regulation's paragraph (c)(1)(i) excepts only publicly traded securities to which (c)(7)(xi)(B) does not apply, so securities that qualify only under the special rule (B) stay within the appraisal paragraph; they remain refused through `gift.section_b`, an over-refusal at worst and no value. (3) Found here: `gift.public_securities` help and source now say to answer No for shares you were not free to sell (Reg. (c)(7)(xi)(C)(1)), which before answered Yes and were computed in Section A without the Section B appraisal.
- **Fix lines:** `gift.special`, `gift.public_securities`
- **Siblings checked:** `gift.allowed`, `gift.deduction`, `gift.no`, `gift.not_public`, `gift.over_5000`, `gift.section_b` (read: gift.section_b (deduction over $5,000 and not public) now carries the deduction test alone; gift.allowed refuses on gift.special then gift.section_b as before); also `gift.special`, `gift.public_securities` (changed by this fix itself)
- **Regression predictions:** no fixture value changes (gift.special is an input). Coverage rows `home.gift_worth_more_than_deduction` (computed) and `home.gift_restricted_shares` (refused by gift.section_b). ## BUG-0716 — BUG-0438 is fixed: the Schedule 1 scholarship question counts the part of a grant paid for required teaching or research

- **Date:** 2026-11-15
- **Closes:** BUG-0438
- **Caught by:** BUG-0438, recorded open; fixed by lane g1-f7a (claude-opus-5-5, judgment). This entry closes it because the inventory is append-only.
- **Source:** p525 p. 35, Payment for services, 'Generally, you can’t exclude from your gross income the part of any scholarship or fellowship that represents payment for teaching, research, or other services required as a condition for receiving the scholarship'; p970 p. 5, Worksheet 1-1, line 9 (taxable part = lines 2, 4 and 8); p970, Reporting Scholarships and Fellowship Grants, 'Include any taxable amount not reported to you in box 1 of Form W-2 on Schedule 1 (Form 1040), line 8r'; i1040gi p. 92, Line 8r.
- **Symptom:** as recorded in BUG-0438, re-checked on this tree: the redraft's prompt asked only 'How much of it was for room, board, travel or anything other than tuition and required course costs?', and its help said only to leave out teaching or research pay on a W-2, so a degree candidate's services part with no W-2, spent on tuition, was left out of line 8r.
- **Fix:** interview/2025/questions.yaml s1.scholarship_taxable: prompt 'How much of it was for room, board, travel or anything other than tuition and required course costs, or was pay for teaching, research or other work the grant required?'; help 'For a degree student only that part is income. A person not studying for a degree gives the whole amount. Leave out pay that is on a W-2. Give 0 if none.' forms/2025/s1.yaml s1.scholarship_taxable source adds 'plus any part that is payment for teaching, research or other services required as a condition for receiving the grant', and its citation adds p525 p. 35, Payment for services. The rare exceptions (National Health Service Corps, Armed Forces Health Professions programs, work colleges) are not named: their service obligations are not teaching or research for the grant, so a recipient is not led to count them.
- **Fix lines:** s1.scholarship_taxable
- **Siblings checked:** s1.line8r (its only reader, and the only line on the same anchor; a choose over s1.scholarship_any, no wording, no change); s1.scholarship_any (the parent tick, unchanged: it asks whether a grant was received at all); s1.scholarship_taxable (changed).

## BUG-0719 — scope.excess_deferral counts section 457(b) deferrals against the 401(k) elective deferral limit (BUG-0548 item 4, re-recorded for scope)

- **Date:** 2026-11-15

The old help sentence 'Your plan administrator tells you' that BUG-0548 also named is gone from the current text.
- **Where:** forms/2025/scope.yaml, scope.excess_deferral (its bank entry, group w2_jobs).
- **Fix sketch:** Say in the help that money put into a section 457(b) plan (W-2 box 12 code G) has its own limit and is not added to the 401(k) and 403(b) amounts; archive the statute or a publication that states it first (Pub. 575 or Pub. 4484), since the archived i1040gi reads 'under all plans'.

## BUG-0721 — BUG-0548 is fixed in part: the SEP and SIMPLE screen names an excess carryover and the job plan only with a SIMPLE IRA; item 1 is not a defect; item 4 re-recorded

- **Date:** 2026-11-15
- **Closes:** BUG-0548
- **Caught by:** BUG-0548, recorded open; closed by lane g1-f8 because the inventory is append-only.
- **Source:** p590a p. 11, Defined contribution plan, "Generally, you are covered by a defined contribution plan for a tax year if amounts are contributed or allocated to your account for the plan year"; p560 p. 11, Deduction Limit for Contributions for Participants, "Your contributions (including any excess contributions carryover)", and Carryover of Excess SEP Contributions; p560 p. 16, Catch-up contributions, "A SIMPLE IRA plan can permit participants who are age 50 or over"; i1040gi p. 24, Line 1h, "under all plans".
- **Symptom:** as recorded in BUG-0548.
- **Fix:** Item 1 (coverage): not a defect. SEP and SIMPLE IRAs are defined-contribution arrangements, and p590a p. 11 makes coverage for one turn on amounts contributed to the person's own account for the plan year, which is what `person.plan` asks; i1040gi's "had a SEP" summarizes that rule. Item 2: the last item of `person.plan_screen` now reads "contributions that are more than the maximum deductible amount, including an excess contributions carryover from an earlier year" (prompt: "including any carried over from an earlier year"), so a carryover refuses rather than being left out; no new arithmetic. Item 3: the screen's other-plan items now read "more than one plan of your own business, or to a qualified plan (such as a solo 401(k))" and "with a SIMPLE IRA, salary reduction contributions or elective deferrals to any other plan" (prompt: "with a SIMPLE IRA, pay you put into a 401(k) or 403(b) at a job"): the elective-deferral limit joins a SIMPLE IRA's salary reduction contributions with a job's 401(k), while a self-employed person's SEP has no elective deferrals and is not combined with an unrelated employer's plan, so a SEP-only filer with a job 401(k) is no longer refused. Item 4: the question it names, `person.sav_excess`, is now the derived line reading `scope.excess_deferral` (form scope); re-recorded as BUG-0719. Item 5: `person.simple_deferral` now says "including any catch-up contributions your plan allows". wording only: no expression, gate, value or refusal of any line changed, and no fixture expected value changed.
- **Fix lines:** `person.plan_screen`, `person.simple_deferral`
- **Siblings checked:** `person.plan_screened`, `person.sep_excess`, `person.sav_simple_plan`, `person.simple_catchup`, `person.simple_regular`, `person.catchup_age50`, `person.catchup_age60_63`, `person.catchup_limit`, `person.catchup_max`, `person.catchup_under50`, `person.comp_after_regular`, `person.deferrals_total`, `person.match_3pct`, `person.match_max`, `person.rate3`, `person.sep_contrib`, `person.simple_age`, `person.simple_age_50_59_years`, `person.simple_age_60_63_years`, `person.simple_age_at_year_end`, `person.simple_age_from_age50`, `person.simple_age_if_open_year`, `person.simple_age_under50_years`, `person.simple_cap`, `person.simple_excess`, `person.simple_open_year` (same anchors or readers; read: `person.plan_screened` reads the screen unchanged; `person.sep_excess` refuses a 2025 excess as before; the computed SEP and SIMPLE lines are unchanged); also `person.plan_screen`, `person.simple_deferral` (changed by this fix itself)
- **Regression predictions:** no value changes in any fixture; a SEP filer with an excess carryover is now refused (none in the fixtures), a SEP-only filer with a job 401(k) is no longer refused by the screen.
- **Tags:** wording; retirement; over-refusal; fixed

## BUG-0725 — BUG-0503, BUG-0546, BUG-0455 and BUG-0569 are fixed: the education credit questions of the person record, the dependent record and Form 8863

- **Date:** 2026-11-15
- **Closes:** BUG-0503, BUG-0546, BUG-0455, BUG-0569
- **Caught by:** BUG-0503, BUG-0546, BUG-0455 and BUG-0569, recorded open; closed by lane g1-f8 because the inventory is append-only.
- **Source:** i8863 (2025) p. 1, Form 1098-T requirement ("can demonstrate that you (or a dependent) were enrolled ... and can substantiate the payment", for both exceptions); p. 2, Table 1; p. 4, Qualified Education Expenses ("nonacademic fees, such as student activity fees, athletic fees ... only if the fee must be paid to the institution as a condition of enrollment or attendance"); p. 4, Tax-free educational assistance; p. 5, Coordination with Pell grants and other scholarships or fellowship grants; p. 7, Earned income, Support, Full-time student; p. 9, Adjusted Qualified Education Expenses Worksheet; ambiguities/2025.yaml amb.2025.edu_1098t_date.
- **Symptom:** as recorded in the four entries.
- **Fix:** Each Part III change is made on both twins (`check_twins.py --sync-from person`), with the declared differences in reviews/2025/twins.json restated. BUG-0503 (1) `edu_inst`: "fees required for enrollment or attendance, including nonacademic fees (such as student activity or athletic fees) that must be paid to the institution"; help: "Required fees include student activity, athletic or lab fees every student must pay the school". (2) `edu_mat` restates the exclusions (2024 or 2026 payments, deducted elsewhere, a tax-free 529 or Coverdell distribution, a sports, games, hobby or noncredit course outside the degree program) in source and help. (3) `f8863.paid` asks about expenses paid "as a student at" a school, "tuition and required fees, or books, supplies and equipment needed for a course of study, wherever bought"; help likewise. BUG-0546 (1) `edu` (gate): counts books, supplies and equipment needed for a course wherever bought; help: "Answer Yes also if the only cost was books, supplies or equipment needed for a course". (2) and BUG-0569 (1) `edu_1098t`: the proof of enrollment and payment now governs both exceptions, as i8863 p. 1 says; the date part of BUG-0569 (1) is not real: amb.2025.edu_1098t_date chose "After February 2, 2026" (Pub. 970), which is the text. (4) `person.edu_half_support` (person only): earned income leaves out a corporation's distribution of profits and caps a services-and-capital business at 30% of the net profit; lodging and property count at fair market value; full-time is some part of 5 calendar months; the help adds housing at its rental value. (5) and BUG-0569 (3) `edu_over`: assistance and refunds "received in 2025, or in 2026 before you file" against the period's expenses "paid in 2025", with course materials as the American opportunity credit counts them for a student who can get it; prompt and help likewise. BUG-0455 `edu_a_this_year`: a scholarship can be included in income only if its terms allow it to be used for other expenses such as room and board, never a tribal-government grant under the Tribal General Welfare Exclusion Act (source, with the p. 5 citation; help in short). The 2026 operations on `person.edu`, `dependent.edu`, `person.edu_1098t`, `dependent.edu_1098t` (source and help) and `f8863.paid` (source) were restated to the new text. wording only: no expression, gate, value or refusal of any line changed, and no fixture expected value changed.
